Description: The Yale Graduate Program in Anthropology covers three subfields: archaeology, sociocultural and linguistic anthropology, and physical anthropology. [11] Sociocultural anthropology provides a range of courses: classics in ethnography and social theory, religion, myth and ritual, kinship and descent, historical anthropology, culture and political economy, agrarian studies, ecology, environment and social change, medical anthropology, emotions, public health, sexual meanings and gender, postcolonial development, ethnicity, identity politics and diaspora, urban anthropology, global mass culture, and alternate modernity. [11] Linguistic anthropology includes language, nationalism and ideology, structuralism and semiotics, and feminist discourse. [11] Physical anthropology focuses on paleoanthropology, evolutionary theory, human functional anatomy, race and human biological diversity, and primate ecology. [11] Archaeology focuses on ritual complexes and writing, ceramic analysis, warfare, ancient civilizations, origins of agriculture, and museum studies. [11]

Requirements: The doctoral program in Architecture offers two tracks of study: History and Theory of Architecture and Ecosystems in Architectural Sciences. Both tracks offer rigorous grounding in their respective fields of specialization while giving future scholars and educators a broad awareness of issues currently facing architecture in its relations with society and the world at large. Program-Specific Application Requirements: A writing sample is required. A portfolio is required for the Ecosystems in Architectural Sciences track; a portfolio is optional for the History and Theory of Architecture track.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences

Description: The doctoral program in Architecture currently offers two tracks of study: History and Theory of Architecture, and Ecosystems in Architectural Sciences. Both tracks aim to educate teachers capable of effectively instructing future architects in their own field and its manifold connections with the culture a tlarge. [12] The program forges a unique combination of professional knowledge with a historical and analytical grasp of architecture, deepening awareness of the field's current state and the critical issues it faces. [12] The History and Theory track provides sound training in historical study and historiography, and cultivates understanding of intellectual trends that inform the reception and role of architecture in the world at large. [12] It prepares candidates for careers in university teaching, cultural advocacy and administration, museum curatorship, and publishing, among others. [12] The Ecosystems in Architectural Sciences track provides preparation in interdisciplinary scientific inquiry, qualifying students to incorporate scientific methods into experimental design frameworks in order to research and develop novel material and informational ecosystems. [12] Students in this track engage in research related to the behaviors of living ecosystems, emphasizing their interconnection with the built environment. [12]

Description: The Yale Astronomy Department welcomes applications for our Ph.D. graduate program. A flew-through highlights of the program are below. For more detail, please peruse our website and feel free to contact our Director of Graduate Admissions. The members of our teaching faculty have international reputations in a broad range of subjects, and collaborations between department members with differing research interests are common. The Department of Astronomy also offers joint programs and opportunities with other departments at Yale and with the Universidad de Chile. With a graduate-student-to-faculty ratio of order unity, close collaboration between faculty and students becomes the norm. Furthermore, Yale students have access to world-class observational and computational facilities which allows them to execute cutting-edge research early on in their careers. The average time for a Yale Astronomy student to finish a PhD is under six years, roughly a year lower than the national average. We attribute this to the close attention given to students, early research experience, and the excellent resources that Yale Astronomy has to offer. Yale Astronomy alumni excel in their careers, often winning prestigious fellowships and continuing on to tenure-track faculty positions. Last, but not least, Yale and its host city of New Haven offers rich opportunities for cultural, gastronomical and extra-curricular activities. Yale Astronomy Graduate students enjoy spending time with each other both in planned activities, such as the weekly Astronomy Happy Hour, group bike rides, running marathons, and cookouts, as well as other more spontaneous get-togethers.

Description: For more than half a century, Yale's Department of Comparative Literature has been a leading institution for the comparative study of literary history, analysis, and theory. [2] The department is committed to a broad geographical and intellectual scope in its graduate curriculum. [2] It introduces students to the study of literature beyond national or linguistic boundaries, exploring its theory, interpretation, and criticism. [3] The program also investigates literature's interactions with other fields such as visual and material culture, linguistics, film, psychology, law, and philosophy. [3] The comparative approach encourages the exploration of transnational phenomena, including literary periods like the Renaissance, Romanticism, and Modernism, as well as different genres and modes of discourse. [3] The Ph.D. program prepares candidates to teach comparative literature and the national literature(s) in which they specialize. [3]

ProgramName: PhD in Computational Biology and Bioinformatics
Requirements: Applicants to the PhD in Computational Biology and Biomedical Informatics must apply through the Biological and Biomedical Sciences (BBS) Program. A Statement of Purpose of 500-1000 words is required. Applicants should discuss their motivation for conducting research, provide a detailed summary of their research experience and how it prepares them for doctoral study, and include how they have taken initiative on a research project, academic endeavor, or employment responsibility. The statement should also describe their career aspirations. [6] Three letters of recommendation are required. The GRE is not accepted. [5, 6] TOEFL or IELTS scores are required for most non-native English-speaking applicants.
Description: Computational biology and biomedical informatics (CB&B) is a rapidly developing multidisciplinary field. The past two decades have witnessed a revolution in the biological and biomedical sciences driven by the development of technologies such as high-dimensional phenotypic profiling, next-generation sequencing, macromolecular structure determination and high-resolution imaging, wearable sensor devices, and large-scale electronic health records. These data-generation technologies demand new computational analysis approaches, which, in turn, have given rise to the field of computational biology and biomedical informatics (CB&B). The Yale Computational Biology and Biomedical Informatics program combines research training opportunities in a range of different fields within the biological and biomedical sciences, in addition to the computational sciences, applied mathematics, statistics, and data science. The scope and balance of a student's program are highly individualized. To enter the Ph.D. program, students apply to the CB&B Track within the interdepartmental graduate program in Biological and Biomedical Sciences (BBS). [2]

The department also offers a combined PhD in conjunction with several other programs, including Black Studies, Film and Media Studies, History of Art, and Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies. [8]

ProgramName: PhD in Film and Media Studies
Requirements: Requirements for all PhD and Master's degree applicants include a statement of academic purpose, a list of all prior colleges or universities attended accompanied by unofficial transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a $105 application fee or fee waiver, and a Resume/CV. Description: By design the doctorate in Film and Media Studies at Yale is always undertaken in combination with one of ten other disciplines in the Humanities (African-American Studies, American Studies, Comparative Literature, East Asian Languages and Literatures, English, French, German, History of Art, Italian, Slavic Languages and Literatures). [2] Thoroughly grounded in Film and Media Studies, they become expert in certain of its issues by offering authoritative perspectives and methods that derive from systematic work with the outstanding faculty and graduate students in another Yale department or program. [2] Inaugurated in 2002, Yale's doctoral Program in Film and Media Studies quickly achieved the international stature it enjoys today. [2] Building on a core faculty that had long overseen an impressive undergraduate major, the graduate program attracted incoming faculty who were eager to help shape it. [2] The quality of the students who have applied has been superior, and the large majority of those selected have chosen to study here. [2] FMS, as our Program is now called for short, officially embraces images and sounds from an array of sources and channels, especially as these coexist and intertwine with cinema, something that has occurred throughout its long history. [2] We study that history as well as the challenge and possibilities of “new media,” which we know to be on the minds of graduate students. [2] This keeps Yale's Program vigilant as it looks to the past for cues about ways to best approach the future. [2]

ProgramName: PhD in Forestry and Environmental Studies

This interdisciplinary program is for students with a clear and focused research interest in an environmental topic that requires an interdisciplinary approach. Students in the joint program work with faculty from both YSE and a GSAS department, combining the strengths of both schools to create a unique and highly individualized course of study. The program provides students with the opportunity to pursue research that bridges the traditional boundaries of academic disciplines, and to develop the skills and knowledge necessary to address complex environmental challenges.

Description: The PhD program in History of Art is designed to train scholar-teachers for colleges and universities and curators and other professionals for museums and galleries. To this end, it offers a broad-ranging yet intensive education in the history, theory, and criticism of the visual arts. The program encourages a wide variety of intellectual approaches to the field and a critical awareness of its history and methods. Close engagement with works of art is a founding principle of the department. Students work with the rich and diverse collections of the Yale University Art Gallery, the Yale Center for British Art, and the Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, which are a short walk from the department. The department maintains a close relationship with the undergraduate program, and graduate students have many opportunities to teach, both as teaching fellows in lecture courses and, in the later stages of the program, as instructors of their own residential college seminars.

ProgramName: PhD in History of Science and Medicine
Requirements: The Program in the History of Science and Medicine requires an academic writing sample of not more than twenty-five pages, double spaced, to accompany the application. Normally, the writing sample should be based on research in primary source materials. Please note that the History of Science and Medicine Program no longer requires GRE scores from applicants. Please do not self-report scores or have electronic scores sent to the Graduate School. Scores will not be reviewed. Description: HSHM students are awarded degrees in History with a concentration in the History of Science and Medicine, and they are fully fledged members of the History Department. Most students in the HSHM program are pursuing a PhD, which may be combined with concurrent enrollment in an MD or JD program (at Yale or elsewhere). A one-year MA degree is also available. The HSHM program allows students to explore topics spanning the full range of the history of science, medicine, and technology, and science and technology studies. Instruction is offered in small workshops, tutorials, and research colloquia, and students receive advice and guidance from faculty advisers throughout their entire period of enrollment. The program incorporates many opportunities for professional development in teaching, research, publication, and presentation, and Yale also offers additional ways for students to explore other skills and fields such as exhibit curation, digital humanities, and public policy. The methodological training provided by the HSHM program is expansive and interdisciplinary. The faculty have backgrounds in a variety of fields, including history, the natural and the social sciences, and the performing arts, and they have deep commitments in anthropology, indigenous studies, geography, race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality, material and visual culture, and museum studies. Students work with all kinds of sources—texts, artifacts, interviews—and incorporate social, cultural, political, geographic, environmental, and economic analysis. Students are also encouraged to draw on other disciplines and they may take classes or work with faculty in other departments.

ProgramName: PhD in Immunobiology
Requirements: Applicants interested in the PhD in Immunobiology must apply through the Biological and Biomedical Sciences (BBS) Program. There are no specific courses required for all BBS applicants, but successful candidates typically have an undergraduate background in biology, chemistry (including organic), physics, and calculus. For the Immunology Track, preferred coursework includes biology, organic chemistry, biochemistry, genetics, cell biology, physics, and mathematics. While there is no minimum GPA, strong performance in science and math courses, along with prior laboratory research experience, is highly valued. [2]

Description: The study of the immune system that confers protection against infectious diseases is known as immunology. This intricate system is also implicated in the rejection of grafted tissues, allergies, and autoimmunity. The Department of Immunobiology is comprised of a multidisciplinary group of investigators dedicated to understanding the cellular, genetic, and molecular foundations of these processes. [4] The department's philosophy is based on the idea that solving complex biological problems necessitates the integration of individuals who share a common goal but possess different areas of expertise. [4] Research is centered on the molecular, cellular, and genetic basis of immune system function and development, host-pathogen interactions, and various autoimmune disorders. [4] A Human and Translational Immunology (HTI) section has been established to enhance the application of basic science research to human diseases, aiming to improve the understanding and treatment of human immunological disorders. [4]

Description: A freestanding, in­ter­dis­ci­pli­nary, Ph.D. grant­ing pro­gram of the Yale Grad­u­ate School of Arts and Sci­ences. It was cre­at­ed in 1999 at the Yale School of Med­i­cine to ad­dress the crit­i­cal need for for­mal train­ing in clin­i­cal re­search, which is vi­tal to the ad­vance­ment of sci­en­tif­ic knowl­edge and the de­vel­op­ment of im­proved treat­ments for hu­man dis­ease. The IMP is de­signed to train clin­i­cal in­ves­ti­ga­tors, all of whom at time of ma­tric­u­la­tion in­to the grad­u­ate school have com­plet­ed med­ical train­ing (M.D. or equiv­a­lent) and at least one year of post­grad­u­ate clin­i­cal train­ing. Stu­dents upon ma­tric­u­la­tion se­lect train­ing in lab­o­ra­to­ry-ori­ent­ed re­search, done in a dis­ease-ori­ent­ed area, and/or train­ing in pa­tient-fo­cused or com­mu­ni­ty-based re­search ar­eas. The strong clin­i­cal fo­cus, in­clud­ing for stu­dents in lab­o­ra­to­ry in­ves­ti­ga­tion, is a marked dis­tinc­tion from that of typ­i­cal Ph.D. stu­dents in the bio­med­ical sci­ences at Yale or oth­er in­sti­tu­tions.

Students have the option to apply for admission to one of two tracks within the program: either solely to the PhD in Film & Media Studies or to a combined program track involving one of the following disciplines: American Studies, Black Studies, Comparative Literature, East Asian Languages & Literatures, English, French, German, History of Art, Italian Studies, and Slavic Languages & Literatures. [4] In addition to acquiring a firm grounding in the methods and core material of film and media studies (and, for the combined degree track students, another discipline), all students are expected to coordinate a plan of study involving comprehensive knowledge of one or more areas of specialization. [4]
Accredidation: The Film and Media Studies program does not have a specialized accreditation listed. [7] It falls under Yale University's university-wide accreditation by the New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE). [7, 16]
ScholarshipAmount: Most doctoral students receive a school fellowship that covers the cost of their tuition and provides a twelve-month stipend. For 2025–2026, the stipend is $50,777. [8]

ProgramName: Combined PhD with History of Art
Requirements: A writing sample is required by this program. [9] The GRE is not accepted. [9] For the combined degree, applicants must meet the requirements of both programs. The deadline to submit an application to a combined program is the earlier of the two individual program deadlines, or December 15, whichever comes first. [9]
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
Fees: PhD students receive a fellowship that covers the full cost of tuition.
Fees.1: $49,500 (for the 2024-2025 academic year; however, this is fully covered by a fellowship for PhD students).
AverageScholarshipAmount: For the 2023–2024 academic year, the standard PhD stipend is $48,300.
ScholarshipAmount: PhD students at Yale are normally fully-funded with a twelve-month stipend, a full tuition fellowship, and comprehensive health care. For the 2023–2024 academic year, the standard stipend is $48,300.

ProgramName: Combined PhD with Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
Fees: Every PhD student receives a fellowship for the full cost of tuition.
Concentration: The Program in Women's, Gender, & Sexuality Studies (WGSS) offers a combined PhD in conjunction with five departments and programs: American Studies, Anthropology, Black Studies, English, and Sociology. [2]
Description: The Program in Women's, Gender, & Sexuality Studies (WGSS) offers a combined PhD in conjunction with five departments and programs: American Studies, Anthropology, Black Studies, English, and Sociology. [2] Students pursuing the combined PhD in WGSS will determine their research and doctoral foci in coordination with the directors of graduate studies in WGSS and the partnering department or program. [2]
ScholarshipAmount: On average, doctoral students receive more than $500,000 in tuition fellowships, stipends, and health premium benefits over the course of their enrollment.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in East Asian Studies
Requirements: Required supplemental materials for the application to the Master of Arts (M.A.) program in East Asian Studies include a Personal Statement of Purpose, a Writing Sample, 3 Letters of Recommendation, and Transcripts. [9] All applicants are expected to have completed at least two years (or the equivalent) of college-level language study in Chinese, Japanese, or Korean. [9] The application and all materials must be submitted online. [24]
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
ScholarshipType: Merit-based fellowships, Teaching assistantships, Research assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Arts in European and Russian Studies
Requirements: The Yale Graduate School of Arts and Sciences requires all applicants to submit a Statement of Purpose, three letters of recommendation, and transcripts from all prior institutions attended. For this specific program, the GRE General Test is not accepted. [1] As a requirement for graduation, all students must demonstrate at least L4 proficiency in two modern European or Eurasian languages other than English.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
Fees: The European Studies Council awards generous financial aid packages of various amounts, usually a combination of tuition and modest stipend funding. [28]
ScholarshipAmount: The European Studies Council at Yale University will offer one fully funded fellowship for an incoming Master of Arts student in the European and Russian Studies program, open to a student who is a citizen or permanent resident of one of the Baltic countries – Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. The fellowship will fully cover tuition and costs associated with the Master of Arts program as well as medical insurance. The fellowship will also offer an annual $15,000 stipend. [44]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in History
Requirements: All applicants must submit an online application form. The required components include a Statement of Purpose, a list of all prior colleges or universities attended accompanied by unofficial transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a CV/Resume, and a non-refundable application fee. Some programs may also require a writing sample and/or GRE scores.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
Fees.1: $50,900 for the 2025-2026 academic year. [4]
MinGPA: A High Pass average overall is expected. [9]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in History of Science and Medicine
Requirements: A statement of academic purpose is required of all applicants, with a suggested length of 500-1000 words. [6] For the History of Science and Medicine program, a required academic writing sample of not more than twenty-five pages, double-spaced, must accompany the application; this sample should typically be based on research using primary source materials. [1] It is also noted that applicants should possess a strong undergraduate background in history and/or a science that is relevant to their intended graduate interests. [1]
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
Fees.1: There is no financial aid available for the terminal M.A. degree.
Concentration: History of Science and Medicine
Description: The Graduate Program in the History of Science and Medicine is a semi-autonomous graduate track within the Department of History. The program's students are awarded degrees in History, with a concentration in the History of Science and Medicine. [3, 4] Fields of study include all subjects and periods in the history of science and history of medicine, especially the modern era. [3] Special fields represented include American and European science and medicine; disease, therapeutics, psychiatry, drug abuse, and public health; science and national security; science and law, science and religion, life sciences, human genetics, eugenics, biotechnology, gender, race, and science/medicine; bioethics and medical research; environmental sciences; human and social sciences; physical and earth sciences. [3] The HSHM program allows students to explore topics spanning the full range of the history of science, medicine, and technology, and science and technology studies. [2] Instruction is offered in small seminars, and students receive advice and guidance from faculty advisers throughout their entire period of enrollment. [2] The program incorporates many opportunities for professional development in teaching, research, publication, and presentation, and Yale also offers additional ways for students to explore other skills and fields such as exhibit curation, digital humanities, and public policy. [2]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in International and Development Economics
Requirements: All supplemental materials such as but not limited to transcripts, personal statement and financial statement should be uploaded to the application. Paper copies will not be accepted. [5, 6]
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GSAS)
Fees.1: Students pay tuition for three semesters at YSE, and two semesters at GSAS. [1]
Description: The International and Development Economics (IDE) program at Yale University offers rigorous training in quantitative analysis, preparing you to tackle real-world economic challenges head-on. The foundation of the IDE curriculum is a series of five core classes in which students develop essential competencies in microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics, and development economics. [1]
ScholarshipAmount: The scholarship covers at least 80% of total expenses, including tuition, living costs, airfare, health insurance, visa, and setup costs, with total support potentially reaching up to US$100,000 depending on the program. [20]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Religion
Requirements: Applicants to the M.A.R. program must submit a completed application form, a personal statement, an academic writing sample (maximum five pages, 12-point double-spaced), three letters of recommendation that address academic potential, transcripts from each college or university attended, and a current résumé or curriculum vitae. [8]
Concentration: ['Asian Religions', 'Black Religion in the African Diaspora', 'Ethics', 'Hebrew Bible', 'History of Christianity', 'Latinx and Latin American Christianity', 'Liturgical Studies', 'New Testament', 'Philosophical Theology and Philosophy of Religion', 'Practical Theology', 'Religion and Ecology', 'Religion and the Arts']
Description: Our Master of Arts in Religion offers pathways to ministry, service, or doctoral work. Pursue a focused program of study in your chosen field, diving in deep with world-class experts and fellow students who share your passions, or pursue a flexible, interdisciplinary program that blends theological study with sacred music, literature, and visual culture.
Accredidation: The school is accredited by the Commission on Accrediting of the Association of Theological Schools, and the Master of Arts in Religion is an approved degree program. [15]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Statistics
Requirements: All applicants to the Yale Graduate School of Arts and Sciences must submit an online application. Key components generally include a statement of purpose, a CV/resume, letters of recommendation, and transcripts from all prior institutions. Specific programs may require additional materials, such as a writing sample or GRE scores. Applicants are advised to review the specific requirements for their program of interest.
Description: To qualify for the M.A. degree, the student must successfully complete eightterm courses (with a 2-semester residency requirement unless accepted for part-time study over additional semesters) with an average grade of HP or higher and receive at least one grade of honors. Courses are chosen in consultation with the Director of Graduate Studies (DGS) at the start of each semester. Course selections become official only with the DGS's signature. Courses in other departments can also be taken with permission from the DGS. The minimal requirement is: all students must become acquainted with probability theory, at least at the level of Stat 5380 or Stat 5410. all students must learn some statistical theory, at least at the level of Stat 5420. all students must gain some experience at working with real data, at least at the level of Stat 5300, but preferably at the level of Stat 6610 or higher. [11]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: Applicants to the Ph.D. program in Biomedical Engineering are expected to have a bachelor’s degree in engineering or the physical/quantitative sciences. Students with a background in the biological sciences are also encouraged to apply if they have a strong quantitative background. All applicants must provide a statement of purpose, a resume/CV, and three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required and will not be considered. The program does not offer a terminal master's degree.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Science
Requirements: A completed application for admission must be submitted prior to the posted deadlines to be considered for the desired term of entry. An application fee of $90 is required and non-refundable. Applicants must submit unofficial academic transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, regardless of whether a degree was awarded. Applicants must submit a current Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV) that provides a comprehensive overview of their educational background, work experience, and any relevant skills or accomplishments. Two letters of recommendation are required.
Description: The terminal Master of Science degree program is intended for students who plan to pursue a professional career in computer science. It may be pursued either full-time or part-time. It is also available through the E-prospects program for employees of member companies. The program requires eight term courses of graduate-level work in Computer Science, chosen in consultation with the director of graduate studies (DGS). Students must take at least one course from each of the three primary areas of computer science: theory, systems, and languages/programming. No thesis is required.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Personalized Medicine and Applied Engineering
Requirements: All applicants to the Yale Graduate School of Arts and Sciences are expected to submit a completed application form, a statement of purpose of no more than 1,000 words, three letters of recommendation, a transcript from each prior college or university attended, and a résumé or curriculum vitae (CV).
Department: Yale School of Medicine and Yale School of Engineering & Applied Science
Description: The M.S. degree in Personalized Medicine & Applied Engineering provides pre-med students, medical students, biomedical, mechanical, and electrical engineers, and computer science majors with the tools to develop innovative 3D solutions for personalized medicine. [2] Students learn to develop and apply 3D technology to address surgical and medical conditions with the goal of personalizing health care treatments to improve clinical outcomes. [2] Courses are taught by both clinical and ladder faculty from Yale School of Medicine and Yale School of Engineering & Applied Science. [2] Using high-resolution medical imaging, 3D printing, robotics, computer navigation, and extended reality, students will learn to develop truly custom treatments, patient-specific instruments for surgery, and personalized medical devices. [2]
ScholarshipType: Limited fellowships, external support, loans, on-campus employment, Yale Health Basic Coverage, Federal Direct Unsubsidized Loans, Federal Direct PLUS Loans

ProgramName: Master of Science in Public Health
Requirements: You will need to provide the following with your application for admission: A statement of academic purpose, a list of all the prior colleges or universities you have attended, accompanied by unofficial transcripts from each school, three letters of recommendation, a $105 application fee or fee waiver, standardized tests (GRE requirements vary by program; TOEFL or IELTS are necessary for most non-native English speakers), and a Resume/CV. Some programs have additional requirements, such as a writing sample. [2]
Department: The Master of Science in Public Health is offered through the Yale School of Public Health's affiliation with the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences. [5]
Concentration: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree program in Public Health offers concentrations in Biostatistics, Chronic Disease Epidemiology, Epidemiology of Infectious Diseases, and Health Informatics. [3, 7] Within these, the Biostatistics concentration offers Standard, Data Science, and Implementation and Prevention Science Methods pathways, and the Epidemiology of Infectious Diseases concentration offers Quantitative and Clinical specializations. [7]
Description: The Master of Science (MS) degree program in Public Health is designed with an emphasis on mastering skills in biostatistics, chronic disease epidemiology, epidemiology of infectious diseases, or health informatics. [2] The program focuses on the theory and application of statistical methodology in biomedical science, the foundations behind clinical research in epidemiology and the practice of informatics across clinical and public health domains. [2, 5] The program is suited for students interested in entering the workforce, continuing their education in PhD programs, and for clinicians. [2] The M.S. in Public Health is offered through the school's affiliation with the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences. [3]
Accredidation: The Yale School of Public Health, which offers the MS program, is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH). The accreditation was awarded in 2022.
ScholarshipType: MS students are permitted to serve as Teaching Fellows or Research Assistants. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Statistics and Data Science
Requirements: General application requirements for the Yale Graduate School of Arts and Sciences include a statement of purpose, which should not exceed 1,000 words unless otherwise specified by the program. [2] Some programs may also require or have the option to submit GRE scores. [8] Applicants should check their specific program's requirements for details on the GRE and other materials like writing samples. [8]
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
Fees.1: $50,900 for the academic year 2025-2026. [11]
ScholarshipType: Research Assistant or Teaching Fellow positions are possible but not guaranteed. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African American Studies
Requirements: Application requirements are not specified for the Bachelor of Arts in African American Studies program directly. Prospective students apply to Yale College, not to a specific major. General application components for Yale College include the Common Application or Coalition Application, Yale-specific questions and essays, two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with transcript, and standardized test scores. A personal essay is required as part of the application, but a separate 'Statement of Purpose' is not.
Concentration: Students are required to choose an area of focus comprised of five courses. An area of focus, selected by the student, may be rooted in a single discipline or may encompass broader thematic and/or theoretical frameworks such as critical race theory; Black Atlantic art and visual culture; race, gender, and public policy; and African-American literary arts. [2, 10]
Description: The African American Studies major examines, from numerous disciplinary perspectives, questions of race, culture, and modern struggles for equality centering on the experiences of people of African descent in Black Atlantic societies including the United States, the Caribbean, Latin America, Europe, and Africa, and the global impact of those experiences. [2] Students in the department explore the historical, cultural, political, economic, and social development of Black Atlantic societies. [2] Majors work to become informed thinkers who are intellectually prepared to offer clarity and insight to ongoing academic and public debates centered in questions concerning race and inequality. [2] African American Studies majors become knowledgeable about the history, primary methodologies, and interdisciplinary breadth of the field. [2] Students learn to critique, articulate, analyze, and interpret universal themes concerning both individuals in society and group interactions as they relate to the work of scholars, scientists, writers, artists, musicians, economists, and entrepreneurs. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African Studies
Requirements: Application requirements are for admission to Yale College, not the specific major. Applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, which includes a personal essay, recommendations, and school reports. Yale has a test-flexible policy, requiring all applicants to submit scores from either the ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams. [1, 3]
Description: TThe program in African Studies enables students to undertake interdisciplinary study of the arts, history, cultures, politics, and development of Africa. [4] As a foundation, students in the program gain cross-disciplinary exposure to Africa. In the junior and senior years, students develop analytical ability and focus their studies on research in a particular discipline such as anthropology, art history, history, languages and literature, political science, or sociology, or on topics such as global health, economic development, or human rights. [4] African Studies provides training of special interest to those considering admission to graduate or professional schools or careers in education, journalism, law, management, medicine, politics, psychology, international relations, creative writing, or social work. [4] The interdisciplinary structure of the program offers students an opportunity to satisfy the increasingly rigorous expectations of admissions committees and prospective employers for a broad liberal arts perspective that complements specialized knowledge of a field. [4]
ScholarshipAmount: Varies from a few thousand dollars to over $90,000 per year.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies
Requirements: All students majoring in American Studies must take fourteen term courses approved by the program's faculty. This includes at least two foundation courses in cultural history/cultural studies, a broad survey course in American literature, and two upper-level seminars during the junior year. Majors must also choose one of six areas of concentration and take five courses in that area. [13, 14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology
Requirements: All first-year applicants to Yale College apply for admission without selecting a major. Application requirements are not specific to the Anthropology program. General requirements include the application form (Common Application or Coalition Application), responses to Yale-specific questions, two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with a transcript, a mid-year report, and a final report for admitted students. [2, 14] All applicants are also required to submit standardized test scores. [3, 4]
Concentration: ['Archaeology', 'Biological Anthropology', 'Sociocultural Anthropology', 'Medical Anthropology and Global Health']
Description: The undergraduate major in Anthropology introduces students to key topics and approaches in three broad areas, also known as subfields: (1) the evolution of human and nonhuman primates, including the evolutionary biology of living people; (2) the archaeological study of human societies and cultures; (3) social, cultural, and linguistic dimensions of human life. [2] In addition to gaining a broad understanding of these complementary areas of Anthropology, majors develop advanced skills in one or more subfields and may elect to pursue a formal concentration in archaeological, biological, or sociocultural anthropology, or in medical anthropology and global health. [4] Whatever their path through the major, students learn ways of understanding and engaging with humanity that emerge from the sciences, social sciences, and humanities, and they often complete synergistic coursework in other departments and programs. [2] All students write a senior essay, often based on independent research, and many go on to careers that incorporate anthropological perspectives. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Applied Mathematics
Requirements: Application requirements are for admission to Yale College, not for a specific major. Students declare their major after matriculating. General requirements for first-year applicants include the Common Application or Coalition Application, answers to Yale-specific questions, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with a transcript, a mid-year report, and the application fee or fee waiver. All applicants must also submit standardized test scores under Yale's test-flexible policy.
Concentration: The Applied Mathematics degree program requires a three-course concentration in a field in which mathematics is used. [12] Students currently combine applied mathematics with astronomy, chemistry, computer science, economics, engineering, geophysics, physics, and statistics and data science, but any other discipline with enough quantitative courses may serve as the area of specialization. [12]
Description: The interdisciplinary major in Applied Mathematics is intended for students who wish to study the more mathematical aspects of science or engineering as well as for those whose primary interest is in mathematics and statistics and who wish to become acquainted with applications. [2] Mathematical models are widely used throughout natural science, social science, and engineering in fields as diverse as physics, bioinformatics, robotics, image processing, and economics. [3] Despite the broad range of mathematical settings and applications, there exists a core of essential concepts and techniques used in addressing most problems. [3] The Applied Mathematics major provides a foundation in these mathematical techniques and prepares the student to use them in a substantive field of application. [3] The major is intended for students interested in theoretical and quantitative aspects of the natural and social sciences. [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics
Requirements: Prospective students apply for first-year admission to Yale College, not to a specific major. The general application requirements include the Common Application or Coalition Application, answers to Yale-specific questions, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with a transcript, and a mid-year report. Yale has a test-flexible policy, requiring applicants to submit scores from at least one of the following: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams. [11]
Concentration: The Applied Mathematics degree program requires a three-course concentration in a field in which mathematics is used. Students currently combine applied mathematics with astronomy, chemistry, computer science, economics, engineering, geophysics, physics, and statistics and data science, but any other discipline with enough quantitative courses may serve as the area of specialization. [1]
Description: The Applied Mathematics major is designed to provide a foundation in these common mathematical techniques and to train students to use them to solve problems in one or two fields of application. The major is intended for students interested in theoretical and quantitative aspects of the natural and social sciences. The interdisciplinary major permits a great deal of flexibility in design. It is intended to appeal to students who wish to study the more mathematical aspects of science or engineering, as well as those whose primary interest is in mathematics and statistics and who wish to become acquainted with applications. Core courses are drawn from Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics and Data Science, and Engineering and Applied Science. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Physics
Requirements: Application requirements for Yale College, not a specific major, include: The Common Application or Coalition Application, Yale-specific questions, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with a transcript, and standardized test scores. Yale has a test-flexible policy, allowing applicants to submit ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) scores.
Description: Contemporary physical science and engineering are becoming increasingly interdisciplinary. The Applied Physics major provides a solid foundation in physics, together with the flexibility for students to combine a physics core with a broad range of other disciplines. Students majoring in Applied Physics take courses in both physics and engineering, as well as courses specifically in applied physics. Students completing the program in Applied Physics are prepared for graduate study in applied physics, in physics, in nanoscience, or in engineering, and, with appropriate prerequisites, in medicine; or they may choose careers in a wide range of technical and commercial fields, or in fields such as technical writing or patent law that draw on interdisciplinary subjects.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Archaeological Studies
Requirements: Prospective students apply to Yale College, not to a specific major. General application requirements include the Common Application or Coalition Application, responses to Yale-specific questions, letters of recommendation from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with transcript, and a mid-year report. All applicants are required to submit scores from at least one standardized test, but Yale has a test-flexible policy, allowing applicants to choose from ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exam scores to fulfill the requirement. [11]
Description: This interdisciplinary major is supervised by the Yale's Council on Archaeological Studies. Inquiries about the major may be addressed to the Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS), or the Chair of the Council. [1] The major in Archaeological Studies provides a program of interdepartmental offerings covering prehistoric, early historic, medieval and other cultures and cultural developments in the Old and New Worlds, and introduces students to the analytic tools that facilitate archaeological studies. [1] The major is designed to expose students to a variety of archaeological research perspectives: anthropological, historical, art historical, and scientific. [1] Also emphasized are substantive studies including (1) study of such prehistoric–early historic transformations as the origins of agriculture, cities and states, and early empires, and (2) study of the material culture, art, and architecture of prehistoric, early historic, and medieval cultures, including the iconography of ancient cultures, the relationship between art and society, ancient writing systems, and American historical archaeology. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Architecture
Requirements: To declare the Bachelor of Arts in Architecture major, Yale College students must submit a Declaration of Intent to Major during the spring term of their sophomore year. This declaration, submitted to the office of the Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS), must include the student's name, address, phone number, a list of architecture-related courses already taken, and a statement of purpose. [14] Before declaring, students must complete three prerequisite courses: ARCH 1001, ARCH 2000, and one from ARCH 2103, 2600, or 2601. [14]
Concentration: ['Design concentration', 'History, Theory, Criticism of Architecture, and Urbanism concentration']
Description: The-purpose-of-the-undergraduate-major-is-to-include-the-study-of-architecture-within-a-comprehensive-liberal-arts-education,-drawing-from-the-broader-academic-and-professional-environment-of-the-Yale-School-of-Architecture.-The-curriculum-includes-work-in-design;-in-history,-theory,-and-criticism-of-architecture;-and-in-urbanism,-and-leads-to-a-bachelor-of-arts-degree-with-a-major-in-Architecture.-As-a-liberal-arts-major-in-Yale-College,-it-is-not-an-accredited-professional-degree-program.
Accredidation: As a liberal arts major in Yale College, it is not an accredited professional degree program. [2, 5, 8, 9] For accredited professional degree programs, refer to the requirements of the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB). [2, 5, 8, 9]
ScholarshipType: Yale offers need-based financial aid, which can include grants and scholarships. [2, 3, 5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art
Requirements: Application for undergraduate admission is not to a specific major, but to Yale College. All applicants submit the same materials. Requirements include submitting the Common Application, Coalition Application, or QuestBridge Application with Yale-Specific Questions; an $80 application fee or waiver; recommendations from two teachers and one counselor; a school report with transcript; standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT); and a Mid-Year Report with senior year grades. [10, 15] Students do not declare a major until the end of their sophomore year. [15]
Concentration: ['graphic design', 'painting/printmaking', 'photography', 'sculpture', 'filmmaking']
Description: Students in the Art major develop a critical and practical understanding of the visual arts and design through a studio-based curriculum that organically blends practice with critical thinking and art historical precedents; apply fundamentals of visual art across a variety of mediums and disciplines; relate the practice of making art and design to culture and a wide range of histories, including the study areas of art history and theory; and learn to embody the knowledge and practice of at least one artistic discipline through active search and research. [6] Students may concentrate on a medium such as painting/printmaking, sculpture, graphic design, photography, or filmmaking, and interdisciplinary study is supported. [6] Art majors learn to place their own work in the context of an inclusive group of contemporary art worlds and national and global cultures. [6] This study is a crucial element in a liberal arts curriculum both for future arts practitioners and for those ultimately studying and working in other fields. [6] A key element of the creative learning process is the critique, which is implemented via both group settings and one-on-one studio visits with faculty and visiting critics. [6] Through rigorous practice and regular feedback, a student gains insight into one's own critical voice. [6] Art majors have access to the graduate program by attending regular lectures, critiques, events, and exhibitions that represent a diverse set of art practitioners who regularly visit the School of Art. [6]
Accredidation: No accreditation outside of NECHE's accreditation. [10]
ScholarshipAmount: from a few thousand dollars to over $90,000 per year

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Astronomy
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission must submit one of the following applications: the Common Application, the Coalition Application, or the QuestBridge Application. Additional requirements include: an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two academic teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report with first-semester senior year grades. [8]
Description: The B.A. degree program in Astronomy is designed for students who do not plan to continue in a graduate program in astronomy, but who are interested in the subject as a basis for a liberal arts education or as a physical science background to careers such as medicine, teaching, journalism, business, law, or government. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Astrophysics
Requirements: Prospective students apply to Yale College, not to a specific department or major. First-year application requirements include the Common Application or Coalition Application, Yale-specific questions, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with a transcript, and a mid-year report. A fee or fee waiver is also required. While essays are a required part of the application, a separate 'Statement of Purpose' is not.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering
Concentration: ['Bioimaging', 'Biomechanics and Mechanobiology', 'Biomolecular Engineering', 'Systems Biology']
Description: The major in Biomedical Engineering provides an understanding of the common methods that underlie many of these disciplines, as well as the ability to develop detailed quantitative approaches in one of the biomedical engineering fields. In offering four concentrations (Bioimaging, Biomechanics and Mechanobiology, Biomolecular Engineering, and Systems Biology), the Biomedical Engineering major provides various flexible programs corresponding to a range of student interests. The course structure of the major permits students to bridge basic concepts in the life sciences and traditional areas of engineering, while gaining a comprehensive understanding of biomedical engineering as a field of study. The program provides graduates with an excellent background for graduate study in biomedical engineering and related areas, or in medicine and other health professions as well as for a diverse range of careers in industry, consulting, or government.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year applicants include: one of the Coalition Application, Common Application, or QuestBridge Application with the Yale-Specific Questions; an $80 application fee or fee waiver; recommendations from two teachers and one counselor; a School Report with transcript; standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT); and a Mid-Year Report with first semester/term senior year grades. [10]
Description: Chemical engineering is rooted in the basic sciences of mathematics, chemistry, physics, and biology; a traditional engineering science core of thermodynamics, transport phenomena, and chemical kinetics; a rigorous design component; and an expanding focus on emerging topics in materials, nanotechnology, and life sciences. The discipline has grown from its petrochemical origins to become central to state-of-the-art technologies in microelectronics, alternative energy, biomedicine, and pharmaceutics. The Chemical Engineering program, with two degree programs (see below), is principally focused on basic and engineering sciences and on problem solving. Additional emphasis is on communication, analysis of experiments, and chemical process design. A special feature of the program is the accessibility of laboratory research—most chemical engineering majors participate in faculty-led research projects, often resulting in publication and/or presentation at national meetings. Chemical engineering graduates find a wide range of professional opportunities in academia, industry, government, business, and the nonprofit sector. Many majors go on to graduate programs in chemical, biomedical, or environmental engineering, or to medical, law, or business schools.
Accredidation: The B.S. degree in Chemical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, Inc. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry
Requirements: Prerequisites for the B.A. degree include a lecture course in general chemistry and its associated laboratory, and a lecture course in organic chemistry and its associated laboratory. A second semester of organic chemistry lecture is also required. Students must also complete courses in mathematics, including multivariate calculus, and a two-term lecture series in physics. The major itself requires fourteen course credits, including prerequisites. The standard B.A. degree requires two semesters of physical chemistry, one semester of inorganic chemistry, one semester of quantitative analysis, an advanced elective, and three advanced laboratory courses.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree is intended for students who want solid training in the chemical sciences and intend to study other subjects in which chemical training would be an asset, such as technology policy, economics, the environment, or medicine. [12]
Accredidation: The undergraduate degree program is reviewed by the American Chemical Society to make sure that it meets the standards of an ACS-certified degree program. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: Application requirements for the Bachelor of Science in Chemistry are the general first-year application requirements for Yale College. Students apply to Yale College and declare their major, such as Chemistry, at the end of their sophomore year. [21] All applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. These applications include a personal essay, an activities list, and school reports. Additionally, two teacher recommendations and one counselor recommendation are required. Yale has a test-flexible policy, and all applicants must submit standardized test scores. [13] Applicants may choose to submit scores from the ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams. [13]
Description: The B.S. major is intended for students who plan to pursue graduate study in chemistry or a closely related field. It also provides a strong background for students who intend to pursue a career in medicine or other health-related fields. A B.A. degree is offered for students who want a less intensive introduction to chemistry. There is a separate major in Chemical Engineering.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Civilization
Requirements: Application requirements for Yale College (as students do not apply directly to the major) include the Common Application or Coalition Application, Yale-specific questions, two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with transcript, and a mid-year report. A fee or fee waiver is also required. Students must also submit standardized test scores through Yale's test-flexible policy.
Description: Students pursuing the Classical Civilization major will study ancient Greece and Rome through their history, art and archaeology, literature, and philosophy. [2] The major in Classical Civilization is designed to offer students an opportunity to study an entire civilization from a wide range of perspectives. [3] It is a flexible program that allows students to take a range of courses in a number of departments, and thus tailor their degree to their own specific interests. [3] Areas of specialization include the literature, history, philosophy, religion, art and archaeology of Greek and Roman antiquity from the earliest beginnings in Bronze Age Greece to the Middle Ages. [3] The culture of the ancient world is studied for its intrinsic artistic value, its historical significance, and its power to illuminate problems confronting contemporary society. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classics
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission must submit one of the following: The Coalition Application with Yale-Specific Questions, The Common Application with Yale-Specific Questions, or The QuestBridge Application with Yale QuestBridge Questionnaire. Additional requirements for all first-year applicants include: an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [1]
Concentration: ['Greek and Latin', 'Greek', 'Latin', 'Classical Civilization', 'Ancient and Modern Greek']
Description: The major in Classics is primarily a liberal arts major. It provides a rigorous interdisciplinary education in the literature, material culture, and history that underlie Western civilization and other humanities disciplines; it can also provide foundational disciplinary expertise for students who wish to do professional graduate work. [3] Students develop a mastery of the classical languages, become acquainted with important periods and major authors in Greek and Roman literature, and develop the linguistic, historical, and theoretical interpretative tools to analyze classical antiquity and its relevance in the modern world. [3] The Major in Classics at Yale offers students the chance to study the languages, literatures, material culture, and history of the societies of the ancient world, together with their influence on later periods and cultures right up to the present day. [4] The major is very flexible, allowing students the opportunity to study the languages and cultures of related Mediterranean societies of the ancient Near East, as well as to take courses in Philosophy, Religious Studies, Literature, History, History of Art, and Humanities. [4]
MaxFails: A record that shows three grades of F in a term or over two or three successive terms will normally result in the student's dismissal from Yale College.
ScholarshipPercentage: 54% of students received a Yale need-based scholarship. [24]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Cognitive Science
Requirements: Prospective students apply for first-year admission to Yale College, not to a specific program. The application requirements include the Coalition Application or Common Application, which contains a personal essay. Applicants must also submit Yale-specific short answer questions, an $85 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with an official transcript, and a mid-year report. Yale has a test-flexible policy, requiring all applicants to submit scores from at least one of the following: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB).
ScholarshipAmount: Varies from a few hundred dollars to over $70,000 per year

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Cognitive Science
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission must submit one of the following: The Coalition Application with Yale-Specific Questions, The Common Application with Yale-Specific Questions, or The QuestBridge Application with Yale QuestBridge Questionnaire. Additional requirements for all first-year applicants include an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report (due when first semester/term senior grades are available at your school). [9]
MaxFails: A record that shows three grades of F in a term or over two or three successive terms will normally result in the student's dismissal from Yale College. [26]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Literature
Requirements: Yale requires all first-year and transfer applicants to submit standardized test scores. Applicants have four options to choose from to include their scores: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB). [6]
Concentration: ['Literature and Comparative Cultures', 'Intensive Language', 'Film', 'Literary Translation']
Description: The Comparative Literature major allows students to address fundamental questions about the nature, function, and value of literature in a broadly comparative context. Students read and write about a wide variety of literary works across periods, genres, and national traditions. They investigate ancient and contemporary approaches to literary study, theories and methods of comparison, and the relationship of literature to film and other media. Majors have the freedom to construct a program of study that reflects their intellectual goals. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science
Description: The Department of Computer Science offers both B.S. and B.A. degree programs. The Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science provides a solid computer science background as preparation for work in other fields such as finance, law, management, or medicine. [9] Each program provides a solid technical education in the core of computer science and allows students to take a broad range of courses in other disciplines that are an essential part of a liberal arts education. [8, 9] The common core of computer science courses for the majors includes CPSC 201, and courses in discrete mathematics, data structures, systems programming and computer architecture, and algorithm analysis and design. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
Requirements: Yale requires all first-year applicants to submit standardized test scores. Applicants have the flexibility to choose which scores to include from four options: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB). [17] Applicants who opt not to report ACT or SAT results should provide results from all AP or IB subject exams they have completed. [17] There is no preference for one test over another, and the admissions office evaluates scores within the context of the student's unique background. [17] Strong scores do not guarantee admission, and weaker scores will not automatically disqualify an applicant. [17]
Description: Computer science is the study of computation. It is a discipline that makes it possible to create, access, and transform information. The computer scientist is concerned with the underlying theory of computation, the design of computer systems, and the creation of applications for computers. The department offers both B.S. and B.A. degree programs, as well as joint majors with Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, and Psychology. Each of these programs provides a solid foundation in the principles of computer science. The B.S. programs are more intensive and are appropriate for students who wish to have a career in the computing industry or to attend graduate school in computer science. The B.A. program is for students who are interested in computer science but who wish to have a broader-based liberal arts education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Economics
Requirements: Yale requires all first-year and transfer applicants to submit standardized test scores. Applicants have a choice to submit scores from one of four tests: ACT, Advanced Placement (AP), International Baccalaureate (IB), or SAT. [14] This is part of Yale's 'test-flexible' policy, which allows applicants to select the results that best highlight their academic strengths. [14] Admissions officers do not have a preference for one test over another. [14] For applicants who choose the SAT, scores from the Evidence-Based Reading and Writing (EBRW) and Math sections should be included. For those who opt for the ACT, scores from the English, Mathematics, and Reading sections, along with a Composite score, are required; the Science and Writing sections are considered optional. [14] Applicants can also 'super-score' their ACT or SAT results, meaning they can report their highest section scores from multiple test dates. [14]
Description: Computer Science and Economics (CSEC) is an interdepartmental major for students interested in the theoretical and practical connections between computer science and economics. The B.S. degree in CSEC gives students a strong foundation in both fields, as well as in the area of overlap. It prepares students for professional careers that incorporate aspects of both economics and computer science and for academic careers conducting research in the overlap of the two fields. Topics in the overlap include market design, computational finance, economics of online platforms, machine learning, and social media. The CSEC major requires some classes in the intersection between Computer Science and Economics which are not mandatory for either major.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Mathematics
Requirements: Applicants for first-year admission to Yale College submit the Common Application or the Coalition Application. Both applications require a personal essay. In addition, applicants must provide two letters of recommendation from teachers and one from a school counselor. A school report with a transcript is also required.
Description: Computer Science and Mathematics is an interdepartmental major for students who are interested in computational mathematics, the use of computers in mathematics, mathematical aspects of algorithm design and analysis, and theoretical foundations of computing.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science and Psychology
Requirements: The prerequisite for the major is PSYC 1100. Beyond the prerequisite, the major requires fourteen term courses as well as a senior project. The requirements include eight courses in computer science (CPSC 2010, 2020, 2230, 3230, CPSC 3650 or 3660, and three advanced computer science courses in artificial intelligence), and six courses in psychology (one in statistics, one in research methods, two from the social science point of view, and two from the natural science point of view). [10]
Description: Computer Science and Psychology is an interdepartmental major designed for students interested in integrating work in these two fields. Each area provides tools and theories that can be applied to problems in the other. Examples of this interaction include cognitive science, artificial intelligence, and biological perception. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Computing and Linguistics
Requirements: Admission to Yale College is not specific to a particular major. All prospective undergraduate students apply to Yale College and declare their major at a later time. General application requirements for first-year applicants include the Common Application or Coalition Application, responses to Yale-specific questions, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with a transcript, and standardized test scores. A mid-year report is also required.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computing and Linguistics
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission must submit either the Coalition Application, the Common Application, or the QuestBridge Application. Additional requirements include an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with a transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [4, 5]
Concentration: ['B.A. in Computing and Linguistics', 'B.S. in Computing and Linguistics']
Description: The Computing and Linguistics major provides multidisciplinary training in the computational study of human language, the development of systems for natural language processing, and the automated analysis of textual data in applications in the humanities, social sciences, and sciences. [2, 4] Students learn the foundational tools and methods that underlie this work, including areas of computer science, statistics and data science, and linguistics, and apply them to some empirical domain, through coursework and an independent research project in the senior year. [2, 4] The B.A. in Computing and Linguistics exposes students to the fundamental ideas and foundational techniques of the field, while the B.S. provides more extensive training and engagement in research, preparing students for graduate work in the area. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Computing and the Arts
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts in Computing and the Arts is an interdepartmental major for matriculated Yale College students. The application process is for admission to Yale College, not the specific major. General admission requirements to Yale College include a rigorous high school course selection, grade trends, and cumulative unweighted GPA. [2] Applicants are also required to submit recommendations from two teachers and a school report with an official transcript. [4] Once enrolled, to declare the Computing and the Arts major, students must have taken the prerequisite CPSC 1001. [1, 6] The major itself requires twelve term courses beyond the prerequisites. [1, 6]
Concentration: ['architecture', 'art', 'history of art', 'music', 'theater, dance, and performance studies']
Description: Computing and the Arts is an interdepartmental major designed for students who wish to integrate work in computing with work in one of five arts disciplines: architecture, art, history of art, music, or theater, dance, and performance studies. [2, 8] For students with a computing perspective, issues in these disciplines present interesting and substantive problems: how musicians use computers to compose; the limitations of current software tools used by artists; the types of analyses done by art historians; challenges in designing and using virtual sets in the theater; ways that virtual worlds might help to envision new forms of artistic expression; and lessons that can be learned from trying to create a robotic conductor or performer. [2, 8] For students with an artistic perspective, computing methods offer a systematic approach to achieving their vision. [2, 8] A foundation in computer science allows artists to understand existing computing tools more comprehensively and to use them more effectively. [2, 8] Furthermore, it gives them insight into what fundamentally can and cannot be done with computers, so they can anticipate the future development of new tools for computing in their field. [2, 8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth and Planetary Sciences
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) in Earth and Planetary Sciences provides a broad overview of the field with relatively few prerequisites, especially in mathematics, and a modest total number of required courses. [9] It is designed for students interested in a flexible program, those pursuing a double major, or individuals preparing for careers in fields like law, business, government, or environmental work. [9] The program focuses on applying scientific principles from physics, chemistry, and biology to understand the Earth and other planets. [8]
Description: The Earth and Planetary Sciences (EPS) program, formerly Geology and Geophysics, prepares students for the application of scientific principles and methods to the understanding of the Earth system and other planets. Subjects range from the history of Earth and life to present-day environmental processes and climate change, the deep interiors of Earth and other planets, tectonic plates, oceans, atmospheres, climates, land surface, natural resources, and biota. [3] The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) in Earth and Planetary Sciences provides a broad overview of the field with relatively few prerequisites, especially in mathematics, and a modest total number of required courses. It is ideal for students interested in a flexible program, those pursuing a double major, or those who study EPS in preparation for a career in law, business, government, environmental, or similar fields. [11] The emphasis of the curriculum is on employing basic principles from the core sciences (physics, chemistry, and biology) to further an understanding of Earth's past and present, and addressing issues relating to its future. [3]
ScholarshipType: Scholarships, grants, loans, and student employment are all considered financial aid. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth and Planetary Sciences
Requirements: Application to the Bachelor of Science in Earth and Planetary Sciences is completed through the general first-year application process for Yale College. Required components include the Common Application or a similar platform, responses to Yale-specific questions, two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with a transcript, and a mid-year report. Application is also possible through the QuestBridge National College Match Application.
Concentration: ['Atmosphere, Ocean, and Climate', 'Environmental and Energy Geoscience', 'Paleontology and Geobiology', 'Solid Earth Science']
Description: Majors in the B.S. program in Earth and Planetary Sciences choose from four concentrations: Atmosphere, Ocean, and Climate; Environmental and Energy Geoscience; Paleontology and Geobiology; and Solid Earth Science. [3] The concentrations are suggested pathways to professional careers and major areas of research in earth and planetary sciences. [3] Students may change concentrations during their course of study with guidance from the DUS. [3] The Earth and Planetary Sciences (EPS) program, formerly Geology and Geophysics, prepares students for the application of scientific principles and methods to the understanding of the Earth system and other planets. Subjects range from the history of Earth and life to present-day environmental processes and climate change, the deep interiors of Earth and other planets, tectonic plates, oceans, atmospheres, climates, land surface, natural resources, and biota. [3] Students gain a broad background in the natural sciences, and select a specific concentration to focus their work on planetary or environmental phenomena of particular interest. [3] The four B.S. degree concentrations emphasize hands-on research experience in fieldwork, in laboratories, or in theoretical analyses and computer modeling. [3] While some graduates continue on to research, consulting, or industrial careers in Earth, environmental, and planetary sciences, the major's broad scientific training prepares students for a wide variety of other paths, including medicine, law, public policy, and teaching. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Languages and Literatures
Requirements: The Major in East Asian Languages and Literatures requires at least 11 applicable credits, including a senior essay. A prerequisite for the major is the completion of L4-level Chinese, Japanese, or Korean. The requirements include two courses of L5 Chinese, Japanese, or Korean; one course in a premodern language (Literary Chinese, Literary Japanese, or Introduction to Hanja); three literature-in-translation courses; three advanced courses with readings in the target language; one outside survey course from another discipline on an aspect of East Asia; and a senior essay. [2, 5]
Concentration: ['Chinese', 'Japanese', 'Korean']
Description: The major in East Asian Languages and Literatures provides an intellectually focused and rigorous immersion in the East Asian humanities, allowing students to study three of the world's great cultural traditions in depth. [1] We offer courses that reflect the variety of East Asian textual traditions, pre-modern through modern, and including film, theater, and media. [1] The major is focused on the analysis of literature, culture, and thought, built upon a solid foundation of language study; many of our courses are taught in translation, but students also have opportunities to take many courses in which literary works are read in the original language. [1] Majors select either the Chinese, Japanese, or Korean track, but are encouraged to take courses on the other tracks and to become familiar with aspects of East Asian literary culture that transcend geographic borders. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Studies
Requirements: Application requirements are not specific to the 'Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Studies' program but are for admission to Yale College as a whole. All prospective undergraduate students apply to Yale College and can declare their major, such as East Asian Studies, at the end of their sophomore year. [3] First-year applicants must submit either the Common Application, the Coalition Application, or the QuestBridge Application. Required components include two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with a transcript, and standardized test scores. [19] Yale also requires answers to Yale-specific questions. [19]
Concentration: ['China', 'Korea', 'Japan']
