Description: In the East Asian Studies major, students focus on a country or an area within East Asia and focus their work in the humanities or the social sciences. [1] The major offers a liberal education that serves as excellent preparation for graduate study or for business and professional careers in which an understanding of East Asia is essential. [1] The major in East Asian Studies is interdisciplinary, and students typically select classes from a wide variety of disciplines. [1] The proposed course of study must be approved by the director of undergraduate studies (DUS). [1] As EAST is interdisciplinary, students typically select classes from a wide variety of disciplines. [1] Council faculty offer classes in the departments of Anthropology, East Asian Languages and Literatures, History, History of Art, Political Science, Religious Studies, and Sociology. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
Requirements: For undergraduate admission, applicants apply to Yale College, not to a specific major. All applicants are evaluated through the same process regardless of their intended major. The general requirements for first-year applicants include: the Common Application, Coalition Application, or QuestBridge Application with Yale-Specific Questions; an $80 application fee or fee waiver; recommendations from two academic teachers and one counselor; a School Report with transcript; and standardized test results. Students do not declare a major until the end of their sophomore year. [10, 15]
Concentration: ['Biodiversity and the Environment', 'Organismal Biology']
Description: The Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology (EEB) a broad education in the biological sciences, covering subject matter that ranges from molecules, cells, and organs through organisms to communities and ecosystems, and the evolutionary processes that shape them. The department offers a B.S. and a B.A. degree...The B.A. program is intended for students who are interested in ecology, evolution, and organismal diversity as part of a liberal education but do not intend to pursue graduate work in the discipline, or for students who are interested in a second major. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
Requirements: Application for first-year admission to Yale is available through the Common Application, the Coalition Application, or the QuestBridge Application. Required components generally include application essays, two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with a high school transcript, a mid-year report, and standardized test scores. A resume is not a required component of the application.
Concentration: ['Biodiversity and the Environment', 'Organismal Biology']
Description:
A major in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology (EEB) offers a broad education in the biological sciences. The subject matter includes molecules, cells, organs, organisms, ecosystems, and the evolutionary processes that shape them. Students may choose a B.A. or B.S.degree.

The department offers courses with no college-level prerequisites that are suitable for nonmajors. These include all 1000-level offerings, as well as 2000-level courses that deal with particular organism groups such as fish, mammals, birds, or insects. [2]

The B.S. program is designed for students planning to pursue graduate study in ecology and evolutionary biology, other biological disciplines, environmental science, or to attend medical, dental, or veterinary school. [9] The B.A. program is intended for students who are interested in ecology, evolution, and organismal diversity as part of a liberal education but do not intend to pursue graduate work in the discipline, or for students who are interested in a second major. [9] The two programs share the same prerequisites, introductory courses, and core requirements but differ in their electives and senior requirements. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics
Requirements: A total of twelve term courses are required to complete the major beyond the introductory level. This includes seven economics courses and five mathematics courses. Courses taken Credit/D/Fail may not be counted toward the major requirements. [7]
Concentration: ['Financial Economics', 'Industrial Organization', 'International Economics', 'Public Policy']
Description: ManyYale student, no matter which major they choose, take introductory courses in economics. The department offers three introductory courses: one in microeconomics, one in macroeconomics, and one in data analysis and econometrics. Microeconomics examines how individuals, firms, markets, and governments make decisions in the face of scarcity. Macroeconomics studies the determinants of overall economic activity, including economic growth, unemployment, inflation, and international trade. Data analysis and econometrics teaches students how to use data to answer economic questions. At Yale, economics is taught as part of a liberal arts education, not as a preparation for any particular vocation. However, the economics major provides a good background for many professions. The major in Economics strengthens students’ skills in critical thinking and quantitative reasoning and provides them with experience in the analysis of economic data. These skills are valuable in the job market, both in the United States and abroad. Recent majors have pursued careers in business, government, and nonprofit organizations. Others have entered law school, medical school, or business school, or have gone on to graduate work in economics, often after working in a related field for two or three years.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Mathematics
Requirements: The primary requirements for the 'Economics and Mathematics' major at Yale are completing prerequisite courses. These include MATH 1200; ECON 1110 or 1115; and ECON 1111 or 1116. [2] Beyond the prerequisites, a total of twelve term courses are required, split between seven in economics and five in mathematics. [2] There is no separate application process to be admitted into the major that would require documents like a resume or statement of purpose.
Fees: The estimated tuition for the 2026-27 academic year is $72,500. [1]
Description: The Economics and Mathematics major is intended for students with a strong interest in both mathematics and economics, and for students who may pursue a graduate degree in economics.
AverageScholarshipAmount: The average Yale need-based scholarship is over $50,000. [8]
ScholarshipAmount: Yale Scholarships can vary from a few hundred dollars to over $70,000 per year. [8]
ScholarshipType: Yale Scholarship grants are awarded based on demonstrated financial need; the university does not offer merit-based scholarships. [19]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: Yale does not have specific application requirements for the Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering program itself. Instead, prospective students apply to Yale College and then declare their major. General first-year application requirements include the Common Application or Coalition Application, responses to Yale-specific questions, two teacher recommendations, a counselor recommendation, a high school transcript, and standardized test scores. [6, 7] A mid-year report and final school report are also required. [16]
Department: Yale School of Engineering & Applied Science
Description: The accredited program leading to the degree of Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering is intended to qualify students to begin a professional career in electrical engineering or to proceed to advanced study. [1] Students may study a wide variety of topics including power systems, semiconductor integrated circuits, VLSI design, biomedical instrumentation, telecommunications, microwave circuits and antenna systems, optoelectronics and materials, digital image processing, semiconductor materials, signal processing, computer architecture, parallel processing, computer systems and multimedia. [1]
Accredidation: The BS in Electrical Engineering (BSEE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and Program Criteria for Electrical, Computer, Communications, Telecommunication(s) and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Requirements: Application requirements are for admission to Yale College, not to a specific major. Majors are typically declared after the first or second year. First-year applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. These applications include a personal essay and questions specific to Yale. Required documents include a high school transcript, a school report with a counselor recommendation, and two teacher recommendations. For standardized testing, Yale has a test-flexible policy, requiring all applicants to submit scores from at least one of the following: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams. [15]
Description: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science is an interdepartmental major designed for students who want to integrate work in these two fields. It covers discrete and continuous mathematics, algorithm analysis and design, digital and analog circuits, signals and systems, systems programming, and computer engineering. It provides coherence in its core program, but allows flexibility to pursue technical electives.
Accredidation: Students interested in pursuing an ABET-accredited degree should consider the B.S. program in Electrical Engineering. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Sciences (Chemical)
Description: The B.S. in Engineering Sciences (Chemical) degree program provides a strong background in the discipline while simultaneously offering additional opportunities for students to enroll in courses in other disciplines perhaps in pursuit of a dual degree. [4] Chemical engineering is rooted in the basic sciences of mathematics, chemistry, physics, and biology; a traditional engineering science core of thermodynamics, transport phenomena, and chemical kinetics; a rigorous design component; and an expanding focus on emerging topics in materials, energy and the environment nanotechnology, and life sciences. [4]
Accredidation: The B.S. in Engineering Sciences (Chemical) is not the ABET-accredited degree. Yale offers a separate B.S. in Chemical Engineering that is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Engineering Sciences (Electrical)
Requirements: Application requirements are not specific to the major but are for admission to Yale College. All applicants for first-year admission must submit one of the following: The Coalition Application, the Common Application, or the QuestBridge Application, each with Yale-Specific Questions. Additional requirements include an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two academic teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report with first-semester senior year grades. [8]
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Engineering Sciences (Electrical) is appropriate for those planning a career in fields such as business, law, or medicine where scientific and technical knowledge is likely to be useful. [2] Often chosen as a second major, this option requires substantially fewer engineering courses and is suitable for careers outside technology in which a student nevertheless benefits from an appreciation of electrical engineering perspectives. [4] It is designed for students planning careers in business, law, medicine, journalism, or politics who want their liberal arts education to include the study of the impact that science and technology have on society. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Sciences (Electrical)
Requirements: Yale requires all first-year applicants to submit standardized test scores, but allows applicants to choose which scores to report from four options: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB). [10] Applicants choosing to submit AP or IB scores should include results from all subject exams completed. [10] General application components typically include the Common Application, recommendations from teachers and a counselor, a school report with an official transcript, and application essays.
Description: The B.S. in Engineering Sciences (Electrical) provides similar technical exposure and equivalent rigor as the ABET-accredited B.S. in Electrical Engineering program, while retaining the flexibility for students to take a broader range of courses than those mandated by the ABET curriculum. [3, 4] This program is suitable for careers in technology and is a popular choice for those choosing academic, industrial, or entrepreneurial career paths. [3, 4] The Electrical Engineering field at Yale broadly encompasses disciplines such as microelectronics, photonics, computer engineering, signal processing, control systems, and communications. [4] This degree option requires a somewhat smaller number of courses than the ABET-accredited B.S. degree in exchange for more flexibility in course selection. [5]
Accredidation: The B.S. in Engineering Sciences (Electrical) is a non-ABET accredited program. [8]
ScholarshipType: Need-based aid, including scholarships, grants, loans, and work-study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Engineering Sciences (Environmental)
Requirements: Application to Yale is through the Common Application or Coalition Application. General requirements include the application form, two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with a transcript, and a mid-year report. Yale-specific questions are also required. A personal essay (statement of purpose) is a standard part of the application.
Concentration: The B.A. degree program allows for elective courses that can build towards an optional concentrated area of emphasis, including (a) Climate and Energy, (b) Environmental Science and Technology, (c) Sustainability and Policy, and (d) Self-designed. [16]
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) degree program in Engineering Sciences (Environmental) is intended for students whose careers will involve, but not be dominated by, the skills of environmental engineering. [3] It is appropriate for those considering a career in fields like law, business, medicine, or public service, where scientific and technological problems play a significant role. [3, 10] The program covers the scientific assessment and development of engineering solutions to environmental issues affecting land, water, and air (the biosphere). [3] It addresses a wide range of environmental challenges, including the safety of drinking water, wastewater treatment, air pollution, climate change, waste disposal, and the development of sustainable water and energy strategies. [10] Students gain a broad understanding of engineering disciplines as well as chemistry, biology, geology, and economics to address these complex issues. [3]
Accredidation: The B.A. in Engineering Sciences (Environmental) is described as a non-ABET program. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Engineering Sciences (Mechanical)
Requirements: Application to the Bachelor of Arts in Engineering Sciences (Mechanical) program is part of the general application to Yale College. Students apply to Yale College and declare their major later. The application process is holistic, and admissions officers consider standardized test scores and transcripts together. [4] Officers evaluate scores within each student's unique context to augment other academic indicators in the application, such as the high school transcript, honors and awards, and educational experiences outside the classroom. [4]
Description: In a society with increasing levels of technical sophistication, a well-rounded individual must have some background in science and technology. The non-ABET B.A. program is designed for students who may be planning careers in business, law, economics, medicine, journalism, or politics but need to understand the impact that science and technology can have on society at large. [2] An understanding of engineering methods and practices, combined with a traditional liberal arts education, provides a strong background for a variety of careers. [2] This degree program offers the greatest curricular flexibility, requiring only eight courses beyond the prerequisites. [1] It is suitable for students seeking exposure to some mechanical engineering training within a liberal arts framework. [1]
ScholarshipAmount: Varies from a few hundred dollars to over $80,000 per year

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Sciences (Mechanical)
Requirements: All first-year applicants must submit a Common Application, Coalition Application, or QuestBridge Application. The application includes two essays and activities sections. Required documents include two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with a transcript, and a mid-year report. Yale has a test-flexible policy, meaning applicants must submit scores from at least one of the following: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB).
Description: The B.S. degree program in Engineering Sciences (Mechanical) is a non-ABET accredited program designed for students who want to gain significant expertise in mechanical engineering while combining their studies with related disciplines. [9, 13] This program is suitable for those who wish to have a strong background in mechanical engineering with the flexibility to take additional courses in other scientific and engineering fields, the liberal arts, or social sciences. [9] For instance, students might pair mechanical engineering courses that focus on structural mechanics with architecture courses, or combine computer-aided design engineering courses with programming courses from the Computer Science department. [9] The curriculum offers a slightly reduced engineering commitment compared to the ABET-accredited B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, but still maintains a solid technical core. [13] It is often chosen by students who decide to pursue engineering later in their academic career, making it challenging to complete all ABET requirements in the remaining time. [13] The program balances in-depth engineering knowledge with the adaptability for wider intellectual exploration. [13]
Accredidation: The B.S. degree program in Engineering Sciences (Mechanical) is a non-ABET degree program. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission must submit either The Coalition Application, The Common Application, or The QuestBridge Application, along with Yale-Specific Questions. Additional requirements include an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [3]
Concentration: Writing Concentration
Description: The undergraduate program in English cultivates students' powers of argument and analysis while developing their understanding of important works of English, American, and world literatures in English. [17] Courses offered by the department are designed to teach students foundational research and writing skills; to provide historical perspectives from which to read and analyze literary works; and to deepen students' insight into their own experience. [17] For students interested in creative writing, the department offers an array of courses taught by renowned professional writers in all of the major genres, including fiction, poetry, play and film writing, nonfiction prose, and journalism. [17] The analytic talents and the writing and speaking skills honed in the major can lead graduates to careers in fields such as advocacy, publishing, teaching, the arts, law, venture capital, medicine, and policy making. [17]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering
Requirements: Applicants to Yale College apply through the Common Application, Coalition Application, or QuestBridge Application. These applications include a personal essay, lists of extracurricular activities, and responses to Yale-specific questions. In addition to the application form, requirements include recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with transcript, and a mid-year report.
Department: Department of Chemical and Environmental Engineering
Concentration: ['Climate and Energy', 'Environmental Science and Technology', 'Sustainability and Policy', 'Self-designed']
Description: The B.S. degree program in Environmental Engineering is designed for students who desire a strong background in environmental engineering leading to a career in the field. The B.A. degree program in Engineering Sciences (Environmental) is intended for students whose careers will involve, but not be dominated by, the skills of environmental engineering. The B.A. program is appropriate for those contemplating a career in which scientific and technological problems can play an important role, as is often the case in law, business, medicine, or public service.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Studies
Requirements: The B.A. degree program requires a total of twelve course credits, including seven core courses and five electives. The core courses include an introductory course, a course in the physical sciences, a course in the life sciences, a methods course, a course in the social sciences, a course in the humanities, and the senior seminar. The five electives must come from at least three of the five areas of concentration.
Concentration: ['biodiversity and conservation', 'climate change and energy', 'environmental humanities', 'environmental justice', 'environmental policy', 'food and agriculture', 'human health and environment', 'sustainability and natural resources', 'urban environments']
Description: Environmental Studies oﬀers the opportunity to examine human relations with their environments from diverse perspectives. [11] The major encourages interdisciplinary study in (1) social sciences, including anthropology, political science, law, economics, and ethics; (2) humanities, to include history, literature, religion, and the arts; and (3) natural sciences, such as biology, ecology, human health, geology, and chemistry. [11] Students work with faculty advisers and the directors of undergraduate studies (DUS) to concentrate on some of the most pressing environmental and sustainability problems of our time: energy and climate change, food and agriculture, urbanism, biodiversity and conservation, human health, sustainable natural resource management, justice, markets, and governance. [11] Students may pursue either a B.A. or a B.S. degree within Environmental Studies. [11] The B.A. program is intended for students who wish to concentrate in the social sciences and humanities. [11] The B.S. program is intended for students interested in the natural sciences, especially fields such as environmental health and medicine, ecology, energy and climate change. [11] Both degree programs culminate in a senior essay project that is commonly preceded by independent summer research. [11] Students must declare a major in Environmental Studies before the end of the second term of junior year. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Studies
Requirements: Application requirements are for admission to Yale College, not a specific major. All first-year applicants must submit one of the following: the Common Application, the Coalition Application, or the QuestBridge Application. Required components include an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with an official transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report with senior year grades. [11]
Description: Environmental Studies is an interdisciplinary major that aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of environmental problems and the tools to address them. Students in the major are expected to draw on its curriculum to develop a sophisticated understanding of the scientific and social-ramifications of environmental problems and the ability to address these problems through a variety of approaches. The curriculum is designed to provide a common intellectual foundation for all majors, as well as the opportunity for each student to pursue a course of study in a particular area of concentration. Areas of concentration for the major include ecology and evolutionary biology, environmental chemistry, environmental engineering, environmental justice, environmental policy, food and agriculture, human health and environment, and sustainable development.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Ethics, Politics, and Economics
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission to Yale College submit the same general application materials. [8] There are no separate application requirements for the Bachelor of Arts in Ethics, Politics, and Economics, as students do not declare a major until their sophomore year. [8] Required application components include the Common Application or Coalition Application, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with a transcript, standardized test results (ACT, SAT, AP, or IB), and a mid-year report. [2]
Concentration: Each student defines an area of concentration. Examples of possible areas of concentration include: distributive justice, government regulation of market economies, environmental policy, philosophy of law, gender relations, democracy and multiculturalism, contemporary approaches to public policy, war and coercion, war crimes and crimes against humanity, medical ethics, international political economy, philosophy of the social sciences, social theory and ethics, cultural analysis and political thought, and civil society and its normative implications. [5]
Description: The major in Ethics, Politics, and Economics joins the analytic rigor of the social sciences and the enduring normative questions of philosophy to promote an integrative and critical understanding of the institutions, practices, and policies that shape the contemporary world. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Ethnicity, Race, and Migration
Requirements: Students must complete twelve term courses in Ethnicity, Race, and Migration, including the senior requirement. [3, 9] There are no prerequisites. [3, 8] The twelve courses normally include ER&M 2000 (Introduction to Ethnicity, Race, and Migration) and ER&M 3000 (Comparative Ethnic Studies). [3, 9] Prospective majors must consult the director of undergraduate studies (DUS) to discuss a study plan and get permission to enroll in the major prior to the fall semester of their junior year. [3, 5]
Concentration: In consultation with the Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS), each student defines an area of concentration. [8, 13]
Description: The program in Ethnicity, Race, and Migration enables students to engage in an interdisciplinary, comparative study of forces that have created a multicultural, multiethnic, and multiracial world. [3, 4] The major emphasizes familiarity with the intellectual traditions and debates surrounding the concepts of indigeneity, ethnicity, nationality, and race; grounding in both the history of migration and its contemporary manifestations; and knowledge of and direct engagement with the cultures, structures, and peoples formed by these migrations. [1, 4, 13] Founded in 1998, the program provides undergraduates with the methodological and practical tools for leadership in a diverse and dynamic twenty-first century. [3] Students study global change from the bottom up, learning about the histories, contemporary experiences, and cultural imaginations of those who have faced displacement and dispossession in many countries of the world. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Media Studies
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year applicants to Yale College are not listed under the specific major but are handled through the central undergraduate admissions office. Yale accepts the Common Application, which includes a personal essay, a list of extracurricular activities, and information about a student's background. In addition to the application form, students must submit a school report with a counselor recommendation, two teacher recommendations, and official transcripts. Yale also requires applicants to answer several Yale-specific short-answer questions.
Concentration: Intensive Major
Description: The major in Film and Media Studies focuses on the history, theory, criticism, and production of cinema and other moving-image media. [3] Courses examine cinema and the broader landscape of audiovisual media as significant modern art forms, and the contributions of moving-image media as cultural and communicative practices of enduring social significance. [3] As an interdisciplinary program, Film and Media Studies offers a wide range of courses, many of them cross-listed with other departments and programs, that give students a broad and deep understanding of the field. The curriculum is structured to provide a solid basis for all majors in the theory and history of moving-image media in the first two years of study, while also allowing for specialization and focus in the final two years. Students are encouraged to take courses in both critical studies and creative production, as each practice informs the other. Course offerings cover a wide range of world cinemas and a variety of theoretical and critical approaches. Majors in their senior year may, with permission of the faculty, pursue a senior project in filmmaking, screenwriting, or a written essay.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in French
Requirements: Application to the Bachelor of Arts in French falls under the general undergraduate admissions process for Yale College. Applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application. For the 2025-2026 admission cycle, Yale has a test-flexible policy, requiring all applicants to submit scores from at least one of the following: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB).
Concentration: Translation concentration. [3]
Description: The major in French is a liberal arts major, designed for those who wish to study French-language literatures, arts, and cultures in depth. [3] The department offers courses devoted to authors, works, and literary and cultural movements that span ten centuries and four continents. [3] The curriculum also includes interdisciplinary courses on relations between literature and other areas of study such as history, law, medicine, religion, philosophy, politics, business, translation, and the arts. [3] Majors are encouraged to explore all periods and genres of literature in French, as well as a wide variety of critical approaches. [3] The French major provides ideal preparation for careers in a range of fields from law and diplomacy to journalism, teaching, academia, publishing, business, and the arts. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in German Studies
Requirements: Application requirements for undergraduate admission to Yale College (the pathway to a Bachelor of Arts) include the Common Application or Coalition Application, Yale-specific questions and essays, two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with transcript, and a mid-year report. A resume is not explicitly required, as activities are listed on the application. A statement of purpose is not required; instead, applicants write personal essays based on provided prompts. Following a test-flexible policy, all applicants must submit scores from either the ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams. [1]
Concentration: ['literature', 'media and media theory', 'history and politics', 'critical thought', 'aesthetics and the arts']
Description: The major in German Studies provides students the opportunity to gain deep competence in the German language while learning to read celebrated literature; to analyze distinctive artworks in a variety of media; to understand key thinkers and writers who laid the groundwork for modernity; and to explore the political, linguistic, and cultural history of Germany, Austria, Switzerland, and neighboring lands. [2] The German faculty works closely with undergraduates to develop their special areas of interest within the rich currents of German culture. [2] German language courses emphasize listening, speaking, reading, and writing in interaction with authentic cultural materials. [14] The curriculum also introduces students to the basic questions and methods of literary criticism, with a focus on rigorous reading practices for a wide range of works from different genres, disciplines, and historical moments. [14] Pioneers in philosophy, political theory, sociology, psychology, history, classical philology, the visual arts, architecture, and music wrote and thought in German, as did founders of the modern natural and practical sciences. [14] Majors discover Kant, Goethe, Beethoven, Einstein, Freud, Kafka, Arendt, and many other thinkers and writers who laid the groundwork for modernity and still hold keys to understanding it. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global Affairs
Bachelor of Arts in Greek, Ancient and Modern
Description: The major in Ancient and Modern Greek is designed to offer students an opportunity to integrate the study of post-classical Greek language, history, and culture into the departmental program in Ancient Greek and Classical Civilization.
MaxFails: A student is not in academic good standing if their record shows three grades of F in a term or over two or three successive terms. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year applicants to Yale College include the Common Application or Coalition Application, an $85 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with a transcript, and standardized test scores. Yale's test-flexible policy allows applicants to submit scores from the ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams. [8, 13]
Description: The history department offers courses in nearly every region, period, and field of the global past. To assist students in choosing courses of particular interest, we have designed “Pathways” that focus on certain intellectual themes across a broad range of geographic areas. Students do not need to commit to a particular pathway in order to become history majors or to enroll in history course... Rather, these pathways are designed to be helpful guides to available courses in areas of special strength within the Yale history department. Each pathway offers a brief overview of its major themes and lists courses with substantial content related to those areas.
ScholarshipAmount: Varies from a few thousand dollars to over $90,000 per year

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History of Art
Description: Art history is the study of all forms of art, architecture, and visual culture in their social and historical contexts. The History of Art major can serve either as a general program in the humanities or as the groundwork for more specialized training. Unless otherwise indicated, all courses in History of Art are open to all students in Yale College.
ScholarshipAmount: from a few thousand dollars to more than $85,000 per academic year

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History of Science, Medicine, and Public Health
Concentration: ['Colonialism, Knowledge, and Power', 'Environment and Society', 'Gender, Reproduction, and the Body', 'Media, Information, and the Public', 'Medicine and Public Health', 'Minds and Brains', 'Science, Technology, and Society']
Description: The Program in the History of Science, Medicine, and Public Health (HSHM) focuses an interdisciplinary lens on the historical and social dimensions of science, medicine, and technology. The program’s central goal is to cultivate a critical and historically informed understanding of how different forms of knowledge and technology have been created in various times, places, and cultures, and how they have shaped the modern world. Majors explore a wide range of questions, such as whether science is universal, the relationship between medical expertise and social inequality, and the nature of technology and its relationship to political, economic, and military power. Course topics include the Scientific Revolution, the history of Western medicine and public health, global health and epidemics, biotechnology, predictions of planetary catastrophe, and the historical development of the physical, environmental, biological, and human sciences. A major in History of Science, Medicine, and Public Health offers excellent preparation for a wide range of careers. Premedical students and others interested in health-related fields can combine preprofessional training with a broad humanistic education. The major also provides a solid foundation for any career at the intersection of the sciences, technology, and public life, including law, business, journalism, museum work, public policy, and government.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Humanities
Requirements: Application to the Bachelor of Arts in Humanities program is part of the general first-year application to Yale College. Specific majors are declared later. General requirements include the Common Application or Coalition Application, responses to Yale-specific questions, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with a transcript, and a mid-year report. All applicants for first-year admission are required to submit standardized test scores. Yale has a test-flexible policy, and applicants can fulfill this requirement by submitting scores from the ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams.
Concentration: Students devise an area of focus according to their interests and with the help of appropriate faculty members. [2] One course is required in each of four areas: literature; visual, musical, or dramatic arts; science in the humanities; and intellectual history and historical analysis. [2]
Description: The undergraduate program in Humanities offers both interdisciplinary breadth and intellectual depth, providing students the opportunity to integrate courses from across the humanistic disciplines into personally meaningful courses of study. [2] Works of literature, music, history, philosophy, and the visual arts are brought into conversation with one another and with the history of ideas. [2] The major in Humanities asks students to begin with broad surveys of foundational works in at least two different cultural traditions, including at least one course on classical Western European texts. [2] All majors take two specially commissioned core seminars, one on the question of what “modernity" is, another spending a whole term interpreting a single work (or small corpus of works) in great depth. [2] Students then devise an area of focus according to their interests and with the help of appropriate faculty members. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Italian Studies
Requirements: Application to Yale College is not specific to a major. All applicants submit the same materials regardless of their intended field of study, and students do not declare a major until the end of their sophomore year. [24] All applicants for first-year admission must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. General requirements include the application form, a personal essay, two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, and official high school transcripts. [19, 21]
Description: The major in Italian is a liberal arts major designed to explore Italy's vital role in the development of the humanistic values and disciplines that have infused Western culture over several centuries. [11] Central to the major in Italian is the conviction that study of another language yields the important benefit of enlightening students about their own culture while instructing them about a foreign one. [11] Core courses provide students with a solid linguistic, literary, and historical background in Italian. [11] The aim of these foundational courses is to provide students with both a broad acquaintance with the major works of Italian Studies and a more detailed knowledge of specific periods in Italian literature and media. [18] Additional offerings range across several disciplines, including the study of film, philosophy, comparative literature, history, political theory, art, religious studies, theater, architecture, and music. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Jewish Studies
Requirements: Prospective students apply to Yale College, not to a specific major. The application requirements are the same for all applicants, regardless of their intended major, such as Jewish Studies. First-year applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. Required components include application essays (a personal statement and Yale-specific short answers), two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with a high school transcript, and standardized test scores. The application fee is $85, though fee waivers are available.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Latin American Studies
Description:
TThe main purpose of the major in Latin American Studies is to further students’ understanding of the societies and cultures of Latin America as viewed from regional and global perspectives. The Latin American Studies major builds on a foundation of language and literature, history, history of art, theater studies, humanities, and the social sciences; its faculty is drawn from many departments and professional schools of the University.

The major in Latin American Studies is interdisciplinary. With two goals in mind—intellectual coherence and individual growth—the student proposes a course of study that must satisfy the requirements listed below. The proposed course of study must be approved by the director of undergraduate studies (DUS). Though all students choose courses in both the humanities and the social sciences, they are expected to concentrate on one or the other.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics
Requirements: Application to the Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics is handled through the general application process for Yale College. Applicants must apply to Yale College, not to a specific department or program. Requirements include submitting the Common Application or Coalition Application, responses to Yale-specific questions, letters of recommendation, a school report with a high school transcript, and standardized test scores. [15] Students do not declare their major until their sophomore year. [26]
Description: The major in Linguistics offers a program of study leading toward an understanding of phonological, grammatical, and semantic structure and of various approaches to descriptive, experimental, and historical linguistics. [9] Linguistics is the systematic study of human language. [3] It explores how language is produced and processed in the mind, how it develops in children, how it is used in society, and how it changes over time. [3] The program also examines the structures of the thousands of spoken and signed languages used globally. [3] Students are introduced to key areas of linguistics and can take a flexible combination of courses across subfields, allowing them to go into depth in one or more areas. [3] The curriculum highlights how language interfaces with the social sciences, humanities, and sciences, and students often take complementary courses in other departments. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics
Requirements: All first-year applicants must submit either the Coalition Application, the Common Application, or the QuestBridge Application. Additional requirements include an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with a transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission must submit one of the following: The Coalition Application with Yale-Specific Questions, The Common Application with Yale-Specific Questions, or The QuestBridge Application with Yale QuestBridge Questionnaire. Additional requirements for all first-year applicants include: an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [6]
Description: The B.S. degree, the intensive major, is designed for students with a strong interest in mathematics who wish to pursue a career in the mathematical sciences. The B.A. degree is a suitable choice for students who are interested in mathematics but do not plan to pursue a career in the mathematical sciences. The B.A. degree can be combined with a major in another subject. For students with a strong interest in the applications of mathematics, or in the connections between mathematics and other disciplines, the department also offers several interdisciplinary majors: Applied Mathematics; Computer Science and Mathematics; Economics and Mathematics; Mathematics and Philosophy; and Mathematics and Physics.
AverageScholarshipAmount: The average Yale need-based scholarship is over $65,000. [5]
ScholarshipAmount: Yale Scholarship can vary from a few hundred dollars to over $90,000 per year. [11]
ScholarshipType: All undergraduate financial aid at Yale is awarded on the basis of financial need; merit-based scholarships are not offered. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics and Philosophy
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission must submit one of the following: The Coalition Application with Yale-Specific Questions, the Common Application with Yale-Specific Questions, or the QuestBridge Application with Yale QuestBridge Questionnaire. [8] Additional requirements include an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [8]
Description: The Mathematics and Philosophy major allows students to explore those areas where philosophy and mathematics meet, in particular, mathematical and philosophical logic and the philosophy of mathematics. [8]
ScholarshipType: Yale's financial aid is primarily need-based, consisting of grants and scholarships. All aid is awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics and Physics
Description: The major in Mathematics and Physics allows students to explore the productive interaction between the two subjects more extensively than either individual major. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: Yale requires all first-year applicants to submit one of the following applications: the Coalition Application with Yale-specific questions, the Common Application with Yale-specific questions, or the QuestBridge National College Match Application. [15] Recommendations from two teachers and one counselor are required, along with a school report that includes a transcript. [15] As of February 2024, Yale has a test-flexible policy, requiring applicants to submit scores from the ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams. [2, 3] There is an $80 application fee or a fee waiver. [15] A mid-year and final school report are also necessary. [15]
Description: Mechanical engineering is the discipline of creating and improving systems for human-kind. [2, 3] A mechanical engineer uses scientific and technical skills and knowledge to design and manufacture products and systems that are safe, reliable, and efficient. [2, 3] Because the discipline is so broad, a mechanical engineer may work on the scale of a jet engine or on the scale of a microscopic gear. [2, 3] A mechanical engineer may work on the design of a prosthetic device or on the design of a manufacturing process. [2, 3] The educational objective of the Mechanical Engineering major is for its graduates to be able to apply the fundamental principles of mechanical engineering in a variety of careers in engineering, science, business, and medicine. [2, 3] Some graduates will pursue advanced degrees and will become leaders in their fields of scholarship. [2, 3] Above all, the major is designed to educate students to become leaders in the conception and realization of important complex systems. [2, 3] The program offers sufficient flexibility for students to explore a broad range of topics or to concentrate on a particular area of interest. [2]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science degree program in Mechanical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org. [2, 3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Modern Middle East Studies
Requirements: There are no prerequisites to the major. The Bachelor of Arts in Modern Middle East Studies requires twelve term courses. These include one course at the L5 level in a Middle Eastern language (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, or Turkish) and two introductory survey courses on the modern period. The remaining eight courses are distribution courses that focus on the culture, thought, history, religion, politics, and society of the region. These distribution courses must be geographically and temporally diverse, draw from different disciplinary approaches, and include at least two courses from different regions or countries within the Middle East, two courses from different departments or programs, two courses focusing on the period before 1750, and two advanced seminars. With approval, up to two language courses below the L5 level may count towards the distributional requirement. Students must also complete a one- or two-term senior essay that utilizes materials in one or more modern Middle Eastern languages. [1, 3]
Description: The Modern Middle East Studies major focuses on the culture, history, religion, politics, and society of the modern Middle East in its full geographical breadth, while developing expertise in any of the major languages associated with the region, namely Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, and Turkish. [1, 2] Courses are drawn from departments in the humanities and social sciences, including Anthropology, History, History of Art, Jewish Studies, Political Science, Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations, Religious Studies, and Sociology. [1, 2] The Modern Middle East Studies major gives students the analytical and linguistic skills necessary to master the complex issues of the Middle East and serves as excellent preparation for graduate study or for professional careers in which an understanding of that region is essential. [1, 2] The major allows students to develop highly individualized courses of study, tailored to their own academic, intellectual, and linguistic interests. [1, 2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Molecular Biophysics and Biochemistry
Requirements: Application requirements are not specific to the 'Bachelor of Arts in Molecular Biophysics and Biochemistry' program but are for general admission to Yale College. Applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, which includes a personal essay, answers to Yale-specific questions, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with a transcript, and a mid-year report. For the 2025-2026 application cycle, Yale has a test-flexible policy, requiring applicants to submit scores from either the ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams. [8]
Concentration: ['Biochemistry', 'Biophysics and Structural Biology', 'Chemical Biology', 'Computational Biology and Bioinformatics', 'Environment and Climate Change', 'Medicine']
Description: Members of the Department of Molecular Biophysics and Biochemistry (MB&B) are united by a common view that processes in biology are understood when molecular, chemical, kinetic, and thermodynamic contributions to mechanisms have been elucidated. [5] Correspondingly, our faculty and students are joined by a shared fascination with biochemistry, physical chemistry, structural biology, computation, spectroscopy, macromolecular engineering, imaging and the molecular basis of disease. [5] Three quarters of our graduates matriculate into PhD, MD, and MD/PhD programs. [5] Other recent graduates have joined companies specializing in finance, management consulting, biotechnology, and pharma. [5] Others have matriculated in law or business school and doctoral programs in the humanities. [5] Still others have performed public service, entered secondary education, or joined the United States armed forces as officers. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Molecular Biophysics and Biochemistry
Requirements: Application requirements are for admission to Yale College, not a specific major. All applicants must submit either the Coalition Application or the Common Application, which includes a Personal Essay. Additional requirements include two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with transcript, and Yale-specific supplemental essays. A mid-year report and final report are also required.
Description: Members of the Department of Molecular Biophysics and Biochemistry (MB&B) are united by a common view that processes in biology are understood when molecular, chemical, kinetic, and thermodynamic contributions to mechanisms have been elucidated. [4] Correspondingly, our faculty and students are joined by a shared fascination with biochemistry, physical chemistry, structural biology, computation, spectroscopy, macromolecular engineering, imaging and the molecular basis of disease. [4] Three quarters of our graduates matriculate into PhD, MD, and MD/PhD programs. [4] Other recent graduates have joined companies specializing in finance, management consulting, biotechnology, and pharma. [4] Others have matriculated in law or business school and doctoral programs in the humanities. Still others have performed public service, entered secondary education, or joined the United States armed forces as officers. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology
Requirements: Application requirements are for admission to Yale College, not the specific major. Applicants declare their major after matriculating. A complete application includes the Common Application or Coalition Application, answers to Yale-specific questions, two teacher recommendations, a counselor recommendation, a school report with transcript, and a mid-year report. The application includes a personal essay and short-answer questions which function as a statement of purpose. Standardized test scores are required, but Yale has a test-flexible policy, allowing applicants to submit results from the ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams.
Concentration: ['Biotechnology', 'Neurobiology', 'Quantitative Biology']
Description: Students majoring in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology (MCDB) receive a thorough yet varied liberal education and preparation for professional careers in a diverse array of fields. [8] The science of biology is extremely broad, ranging across the domains of molecules, cells, tissues and organs, organisms, and ecosystems. [8] Moreover, biology explores questions of evolutionary history and the processes of evolutionary change, as well as the mechanisms by which cells, organisms, and ecosystems function. [8] Practical applications of biology include the development of biologicals and pharmaceuticals, the practice of medicine, and the pursuit of the scientific bases for understanding the development and function of biological systems. [8] Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology (MCDB) offers programs for students wishing to concentrate on molecular and cellular biology and genetics, with applications to problems in cell and developmental biology, neurobiology, and various aspects of quantitative biology. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year applicants to Yale are not specific to the 'Bachelor of Science in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology' major but are handled by the central undergraduate admissions office. While an official checklist is not provided in a single document, the necessary components are described on the admissions website. These include a Common Application or Coalition Application, an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one school counselor, a school report with a transcript, a mid-year report, and standardized test scores. Yale has a test-flexible policy, allowing applicants to submit ACT, SAT, AP, or IB scores.
Concentration: ['Biotechnology', 'Neurobiology', 'Quantitative Biology']
Description: Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology (MCDB) offers programs for students wishing to concentrate on molecular and cellular biology and genetics, with applications to problems in cell and developmental biology, neurobiology, and various aspects of quantitative biology. Interdisciplinary opportunities are available within the major in the Biotechnology, Neurobiology, and Quantitative Biology concentrations.
