Practical applications of biology include the development of biologicals and pharmaceuticals, the practice of medicine, and the pursuit of the scientific bases for understanding the development and function of biological systems.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music
Requirements: Applicants apply to Yale College, not to the Bachelor of Arts in Music major directly. Most successful applicants submit only the required application materials (Common Application, Coalition Application, or QuestBridge Application), which include a personal essay and an activities list. [12] For students with exceptional musical talent, submitting a music supplement is an option. [12] This supplement is reviewed by music faculty and should only be submitted if the applicant's musical ability is a strong and important part of their application. [12, 13] The supplement, submitted via the Arts Portfolio Submission Tool, should consist of two or three recordings of contrasting styles totaling around ten minutes. [13] Yale College does not conduct auditions. [12, 13]
Concentration: Intensive Major
Description: The Department of Music offers introductory and advanced instruction in the history of music, the theory of music, composition, music technology, and performance. The Music major provides a general music program in the humanities, as well as preparation for graduate studies or music careers. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations
Requirements: Prospective undergraduate students apply to Yale College and not to a specific major. The application requirements are the same for all applicants. The 'Bachelor of Arts in Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations' is a major taken after admission. General application requirements include the Common Application or Coalition Application, responses to Yale-specific questions, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with a transcript, and a mid-year report.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Neuroscience
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission must submit one of the following: The Coalition Application with Yale-Specific Questions, The Common Application with Yale-Specific Questions, or The QuestBridge Application with Yale QuestBridge Questionnaire. Additional requirements for all first-year applicants are an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [1]
Description: The Neuroscience major offers a curriculum that is broad and rigorous. The interdisciplinary nature of the major allows students to combine a variety of courses into a cohesive plan of study. The major also offers direct experience in the methods and practices of scientific research through independent study. Students who complete the major are well prepared for graduate study in neuroscience, for medical school, and for careers in which an understanding of behavior, the brain, and the nervous system is relevant.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Neuroscience
Requirements: Prospective students apply to Yale College, not to a specific major. First-year application requirements include the Common Application or Coalition Application, Harvard College Questions and Writing Supplement, a school report with high school transcript, two teacher recommendations, and a mid-year school report. Yale has a test-flexible policy, requiring all applicants to submit scores from either the ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams. [15]
ScholarshipAmount: Varies, up to over $90,000 per year

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy
Requirements: Yale admits undergraduate students to Yale College as a whole, not to a specific major. As such, there are no separate application requirements for the 'Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy'. All applicants must meet the general first-year application requirements for Yale College. Yale requires applicants to submit scores from one of four test types: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB). [6] Applicants submit essays as part of the Common Application or Coalition Application, which serve as a personal statement. [13]
Description: The Philosophy major prepares students to reflect critically and creatively on questions concerning the nature of things, the scope and limits of human understanding, and the principles of value and right action. The major aims to address these questions wherever they arise, whether in the philosophical tradition, in other disciplines and practices, or in everyday life.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics
Requirements: Information regarding general application requirements to Yale University is not available on the specified website, catalog.yale.edu. This site details the academic requirements for students already enrolled at Yale who wish to pursue a major in Physics. These requirements include prerequisites in mathematics (e.g., MATH 112, 115, or 116; or MATH 120 or MASC 120; or MATH 225 or 226; or MATH 230, 231) and physics, as well as a description of the curriculum for both the B.S. and B.A. degree paths.
Concentration: ['intensive major']
Description: To achieve this goal, we offer courses for physics majors who intend to further their study of physics or any STEM field in graduate school, as well as those physics majors who intend to go into law, consulting, financial services, technology industries, teaching, or any number of fields. The overarching goal of the physics program is to train students—majors and nonmajors alike—to think like physicists, the hallmarks of which include: striving for fundamental explanations that have broad predictive power; appreciating that quantitative analysis is necessary for proper understanding; simplifying physical situations to their essentials to enable the development of mathematical models to explain and predict experimental data; and comparing experimental data from the natural world to theory. [11] Many students enroll in our introductory courses as a compulsory requirement of their STEM major; to satisfy a requirement for admission into medical school; or because they appreciate the quantitative training and intrinsic value offered by a basic understanding of modern physics. The department offers two majors in Physics: the B.S. and the B.S. intensive major. [11] Students in either program acquire advanced training in physics, mathematics, and related topics through the core courses. They use electives to design individualized programs with more depth or breadth, depending on their interests. Both degree programs require some research experience. [11] Combined majors are available in Mathematics and Physics, Astrophysics, Physics and Philosophy, and Physics and Geosciences. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics and Geosciences
Requirements: Yale requires all first-year and transfer applicants to submit standardized test scores. Applicants choose which scores to include from four options: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB). [11]
Concentration: ['Atmosphere, Ocean, and Climate track', 'Solid Earth Science track']
Description: The major in Physics and Geosciences applies fundamental physical principles to the study of the Earth and other planetary bodies, synthesizing concepts and methods from both the Physics majors and the Earth and Planetary Sciences majors. [1, 2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Physics and Philosophy
Requirements: All prospective students must apply using the Common Application, Coalition Application, or QuestBridge National College Match Application. The application includes two Yale-specific short essay questions. Required documents include a high school transcript, a school report, and recommendations from two teachers and one counselor. A mid-year report with grades from the first semester of the senior year is also required.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics and Philosophy
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit one of the following: The Coalition Application with Yale-Specific Questions, the Common Application with Yale-Specific Questions, or the QuestBridge Application with Yale QuestBridge Questionnaire. Additional requirements include an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [3]
Description:
Directors of undergraduate studies: David Poland (Physics), Daniel Greco (Philosophy).

Prospective majors in Physics and Philosophy are advised to begin taking the prerequisites during their first year, and to take at least two of the required philosophy courses by the end of their sophomore year. Prerequisites for this major are as follows: mathematics through calculus at the level of MATH 1200; any introductory physics lecture sequence PHYS 1700, 1710 or higher; PHYS 1650L and 1660L, or PHYS 2050L.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission must submit one of the following: The Coalition Application with Yale-Specific Questions, The Common Application with Yale-Specific Questions, or The QuestBridge Application with Yale QuestBridge Questionnaire. Additional requirements for all first-year applicants include an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [7]
Concentration: Students following the standard B.A. degree program, interdisciplinary concentration are allowed to identify and pursue an area of study that crosses conventional disciplinary and departmental boundaries. [12] Examples of interdisciplinary concentrations include (but are not limited to) urban studies, health politics and policy, political economy, political psychology, or a focus on the politics of a given global region informed by the study of the history and society of that region. [12]
Description: Political science addresses how individuals and groups organize, allocate, and challenge the power to make collective decisions involving public issues. [12] The goal of the major is to enable students to think critically and analytically about the agents, incentives, and institutions that shape political phenomena within human society. [12] The subfields of political philosophy and analytical political theory (which includes the study of both qualitative and quantitative methodology) support the acquisition of the lenses through which such thought skills can be enriched. [12] The subfields of American government, comparative politics, and international relations, in turn, allow students to reinforce and refine those skills, while also promoting their application to a wide variety of contexts, whether contemporary or historical. [12] Students may also construct interdisciplinary curricula, which allows them to apply the approaches of the discipline to a topic for which a more complete understanding also involves approaches gleaned from other disciplines. [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Portuguese
Requirements: Application requirements for Yale College, not a specific major, include the Common Application or Coalition Application, Yale-specific essays, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a school report with transcript, and standardized test scores. Yale has a test-flexible policy, requiring applicants to submit scores from at least one of the following: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB).
Description: The major in Portuguese is a liberal arts major intended to develop competence in the Portuguese language and provide students with a comprehensive knowledge of the literatures and cultures of Portugal, Brazil, and African and Asian lands of Portuguese language or influence. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission must submit one of the following: The Coalition Application with Yale-Specific Questions, The Common Application with Yale-Specific Questions, or The QuestBridge Application with Yale QuestBridge Questionnaire. Additional requirements include an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [8]
Concentration: The Psychology major offers a Standard track and a Neuroscience concentration. [8]
Description: The Psychology department at Yale offers a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) degree with coursework and research opportunities in the fields of clinical, cognitive, developmental, neuroscientific, and social psychology. The program is designed to help students better understand human behavior, including who we are, what we do, and how to enhance our lives and society. A foundation in psychology is applicable to careers in education and research, law, medicine and public health, politics and public policy, as well as business fields like marketing, finance, and management. [9] The B.A. degree is typically awarded to students who conduct a nonempirical literature review during their senior year. [9] Psychology can also be taken as a Bachelor of Science (B.S.), which is awarded to students who conduct empirical research. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Psychology
Requirements: The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree is awarded to students who conduct empirical research through PSYC 4990 during their senior year. An empirical research project typically involves designing an experiment and analyzing the collected data. The requirements for the major include an introductory psychology course (PSYC 1100), a statistics course, a data-collection course, two social science courses, two natural science courses, and four electives. For the B.S. degree, students must complete the empirical research course (PSYC 4990) and one additional course from PSYC 4000–4980. [19]
Description: Psychology is the scientific study of the mind. The major provides a liberal arts education, and it is also a preparation for a career in a variety of fields. Within psychology, there are several areas of specialization. For example, clinical psychologists, who have advanced degrees, diagnose and treat psychological problems. Other psychologists do research and teach at universities. Still others work in industry, in schools, or in other nonacademic settings. The Psychology major at Yale provides the intellectual foundation for all of these pursuits. It provides a strong background for many professions, including law, medicine, public health, business, and education.
ScholarshipPercentage: More than 50% of Yale students receive financial aid from Yale. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies requires twelve term courses. This includes a core of five courses, a junior seminar (RLST 4900), a two-term senior essay, and four electives. [5, 15] Students plan their program in consultation with the director of undergraduate studies (DUS). [5, 12] There are no specific high school courses required for admission to Yale College, regardless of the intended major. [9] All applicants submit the same materials for evaluation. [9]
ScholarshipAmount: From a few hundred dollars to over $80,000 per year

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Russian
Requirements: Application requirements for Yale College (not specific to the Russian major) include the Common Application, Coalition Application, or QuestBridge Application; Yale-specific questions; recommendations from two teachers and one counselor; a school report including a transcript; a mid-year report; and the submission of standardized test scores. Yale has a test-flexible policy, allowing applicants to submit scores from the ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB) exams.
Description: The major in Russian offered by the Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures acquaints students with Russian literature and culture, develops students' appreciation of literary values and skill in literary analysis, and gives them a basic competence in Russian. [3] For an area major in Russian studies, see Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies, an interdisciplinary program administered by the Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies
Requirements: Application requirements are not specific to the 'Bachelor of Arts in Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies' program but are for all first-year applicants to Yale College. The required application materials include: an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB, or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [2]
Concentration: ['Russian Studies', 'East European Studies', 'Eurasian Studies']
Description: The major in Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies, administered by the Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures, offers an interdisciplinary approach to the study of a broad region: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, the Caucasus, and central Asia; Poland, Hungary, the Czech and Slovak Republics, and other areas in east central Europe; and the Balkans. [5] Students majoring in RSEE may concentrate exclusively on Russian Studies, or on East European or Eurasian Studies. [5] The major is appropriate for students considering careers in international public policy, diplomacy, or business, and is also suited to students wishing to continue academic work. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology
Requirements: Application requirements are for admission to Yale College, not for a specific major. First-year applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. These applications include a Personal Essay and Yale-specific short-answer questions. Applicants must also submit a high school transcript, two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, and a mid-year report. An application fee or fee waiver is also required.
Concentration: ['Economy and Society', 'Health and Society', 'Data and Society', 'Inequality, Race, and Society', 'Student-Designed']
Description: The Sociology department offers six undergraduate pathways leading to the B.A. degree: (1) the standard major focuses on sociological concepts, theories, and methods; (2) the concentration in economy and society focuses on the cultural frameworks, relationships, and social institutions that give rise to markets and shape economic behavior; (3) the concentration in health and society emphasizes social processes as they affect health and medicine; (4) the concentration in data and society studies methods of analysis; (5) the concentration in inequality, race, and society considers the dimensions of how discrimination shapes society; and (6) the student-designed program combines sociology with a concentration in a different subject area. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish
Requirements: Application to Yale is through the Common Application or Coalition Application. Requirements for all first-year applicants include the application platform, Yale-specific questions, two teacher recommendations, one counselor recommendation, a school report with a transcript, and standardized test scores. There is an application fee or fee waiver.
Concentration: Intensive major
Description: The major in Spanish is a liberal arts major that offers a wide range of courses in the language, literatures, and cultures of the twenty Spanish-speaking countries in Europe and Latin America. The program in Spanish provides students with the opportunity to acquire thorough linguistic proficiency as well as in-depth knowledge of cultural and literary topics. The Spanish major opens up a world of literature, history, philosophy, art and culture, and is an excellent preparation for careers in law, diplomacy, medicine, business, the arts, academics, journalism, and education. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Special Divisional Major
Requirements: The Special Divisional Major is an alternative for enrolled Yale students whose academic interests cannot be met by an existing major. Students must design their own major and submit a proposal to the Committee on Honors and Academic Standing. [8] The application requires an explanation of the major's objectives and organizing principles. [14] The proposed major must ordinarily comprise at least twelve advanced term courses and a senior project. [8] Students must also secure two faculty advisers who will provide letters of support. [8, 14]
Description: A Special Divisional Major affords an alternative for students whose academic interests cannot be met by an existing departmental or special major. [1] Students may, with the approval of the Committee on Honors and Academic Standing, design majors of their own in consultation with members of the faculty. [1] Special Divisional Majors differ so widely in content that there is no uniform format, but many of these majors draw from several departments to focus on a particular culture, period, or problem (e.g., French studies, medieval studies, urban studies). [1] A Special Divisional Major may not be offered as one of two majors. [3] Students considering a Special Divisional Major should be aware of its particular demands and risks, as they face the challenges of interdisciplinary work and must grapple with the conceptual processes of disparate disciplines. [1] They must establish criteria for selecting courses and organize them to obtain an adequate base in the fields necessary for advanced work on a specific topic. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Special Divisional Major
Requirements: To be approved for a Special Divisional Major, a student must design a unique course of study with at least twelve advanced-level courses and a special project. [3, 8] The student needs to secure two faculty advisers, with the primary adviser being a regular member of the Yale College faculty. [3, 10] The core requirement is a detailed proposal demonstrating that the academic goals cannot be met within an existing major and that the proposed program has a breadth and depth equivalent to a standard departmental major. [3] The application must also be supported by letters from the chosen faculty advisers. [10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Statistics and Data Science
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year admission to Yale College are not specific to the 'Bachelor of Arts in Statistics and Data Science' major. Applicants apply to Yale College and declare a major later. General requirements include: submitting the Coalition Application, Common Application, or QuestBridge Application; paying an $80 application fee or requesting a fee waiver; providing recommendations from two teachers and one counselor; and submitting a School Report with a transcript and a Mid-Year Report. [7] Yale has a 'test-flexible' policy, requiring all applicants to submit scores from at least one of the following: ACT, Advanced Placement (AP), International Baccalaureate (IB), or SAT. [3]
Description: The B.A. in Statistics and Data Science is designed to acquaint students with fundamental techniques in the field. The B.S. in Statistics and Data Science is an in-depth program that builds on the B.A. by requiring more courses in the discipline. It is designed to prepare students for graduate study or for a research-related career. Students majoring in Statistics and Data Science take courses in both mathematical and practical foundations. They are also encouraged to take courses in the discipline areas listed below. The B.A. in Statistics and Data Science is designed to acquaint students with fundamental techniques in the field. This field is a natural outgrowth of statistics that incorporates advances in machine learning, data mining, and high-performance computing, along with domain expertise in the social sciences, natural sciences, engineering, management, medicine, and digital humanities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Statistics and Data Science
Requirements: All applicants for first-year admission must submit one of the following: The Coalition Application with Yale-Specific Questions, The Common Application with Yale-Specific Questions, or The QuestBridge Application with Yale QuestBridge Questionnaire. [2] Additional requirements for all first-year applicants include an $80 application fee or fee waiver, recommendations from two teachers and one counselor, a School Report with transcript, standardized test results (ACT, AP, IB or SAT), and a Mid-Year Report. [2]
Description: The B.S. prepares students to participate in research efforts or to pursue graduate school in the study of data science. [2] Statistics is the science and art of prediction and explanation. [2] The mathematical foundation of statistics lies in the theory of probability, which is applied to problems of making inferences and decisions under uncertainty. [2] Practical statistical analysis also uses a variety of computational techniques, methods of visualizing and exploring data, methods of seeking and establishing structure and trends in data, and a mode of questioning and reasoning that quantifies uncertainty. [2] Students majoring in Statistics and Data Science take courses in both mathematical and practical foundations. [2] They are also encouraged to take courses in the discipline areas listed below. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theater and Performance Studies
Requirements: Application to Yale is for admission to Yale College, not to a specific major. The requirements for the 'Bachelor of Arts in Theater and Performance Studies' are the general requirements for admission to Yale College. These include completing the Common Application or Coalition Application, which involves a personal essay, responses to Yale-specific short answer questions, and two letters of recommendation from teachers. Application materials also include a school report with a counselor recommendation and transcripts.
Fees: The tuition for Yale College for the 2026–2027 academic year is $72,500. [4]
Description: A major in Theater & Performance Studies consists of courses that combine critical and creative inquiry and is designed for students interested in not only developing skills in theater and performance but in an interdisciplinary exploration of how these art forms matter in the world. This distinctive degree program engages with theater and performance as it intersects with social justice, cultural politics, criticism, American and world cultures, arts management, education, and more. [1]   The TAPSProgramoffers studio/seminar courses in acting, directing, playwriting, design, technical theatre, and stage management, as well as coursework and production opportunities that emphasize adaptation and performance; devising and developing new work; cross-cultural performance and world theatre history; performance and politics; community- based performance; arts management; ensemble techniques; musical and cabaret performance; interdisciplinary learning about culture, race, gender, and identity; and a variety of special topics that offer diverse opportunities for undergraduate research.
AverageScholarshipAmount: The average need-based scholarship in 2024-2025 was $72,941.
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarships can range from a few thousand dollars to over $90,000 per year. For families with annual incomes below $100,000 and typical assets, the expected contribution is $0. For families with annual incomes below $200,000, need-based scholarships will meet or exceed the cost of tuition.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
Requirements: Application for a Bachelor of Arts degree is made to Yale College, not to a specific major. Students may select their major in Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies after matriculating. Yale requires all first-year applicants to submit standardized test scores. [7] Applicants have the flexibility to choose which scores to report from four options: ACT, SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), or International Baccalaureate (IB). [7]
Concentration: Students majoring in Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies develop an individual area of concentration. Recent examples of concentrations include literature and queer aesthetics; transnational feminist practices; the intellectual history of civil rights activism; AIDS health policies; gender, religion, and international NGOs; women’s health and reproductive justice; and gender and sexuality in early education.
Description: The scholarship in Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies (WGSS) is interdisciplinary and wide-ranging. The WGSS major is designed to foster a critical understanding of the complex ways in which gender and sexuality have been defined and have operated in a variety of social and cultural contexts. The major emphasizes the intersections of gender and sexuality with other markers of difference, including race, ethnicity, class, nationality, and religion. Students majoring in Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies take a series of core courses, develop an individual area of concentration, and write a senior essay. The program encourages work that is interdisciplinary, intersectional, and transnational.
